Title: Mara chairman orders SOP review after missing MRSM Alor Gajah students found
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Majlis Amanah Rakyat (Mara) management has been instructed to review its standard operating procedure (SOP) for taking students to health clinics following the disappearance of two MRSM Alor Gajah students for four days.
Mara chairman Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said a full investigation must be conducted to determine the cause of the incident and prevent a recurrence.
"Whatever the cause of the two MRSM Alor Gajah students going missing for four days, I have instructed Mara management to review the SOP for taking students to clinics to prevent similar incidents.
"A full investigation must also be conducted," he said in a Facebook post today.
Asyraf previously confirmed that the two 16-year-old students, reported missing since Aug 11, were found safe at Central Market here last night.
Before they were reported missing, both students had sought treatment at a health clinic in Alor Gajah after feeling unwell.
Following the incident, numerous social media users shared comments regarding the current SOP for bringing MRSM students to clinics for medical treatment.
Some users claimed there was no fixed requirement for teachers to accompany students for medical visits, while others asserted that doing so fell outside a teacher's duties.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Titiwangsa pond dries up during maintenance, rain restores water level
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A pond at Titiwangsa Lake Gardens here appeared to have dried up, sparking public concern after images of the site went viral on social media.
However, a check found that only the pond near the children's playground had been affected, while the main lake remained unaffected, contrary to claims in social media posts circulating since the day before.
The pond was drained as part of maintenance work being carried out by a contractor, with the area cordoned off with red tape.
A notice issued by Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) also informed the public that maintenance work was underway.
Heavy rain yesterday subsequently caused the pond to fill with water again.
Visitor Peaceca Anak Cally, 25, said the dry pond had somewhat affected the scenery and image of Titiwangsa Lake Gardens, one of the city's popular recreational spots.
"DBKL should explain why the pond was drained so that the public understands the situation.
"If possible, the maintenance work should be completed quickly as the area is used by the public for recreation and sports activities," she told Harian Metro.
Another visitor, Nur Aida Zulrushdi, 22, said the situation had not affected recreational activities but had slightly diminished the area's scenic appeal.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: AUKU abolition to be brought to Cabinet on Wednesday, says Anwar
Article:
AYER KEROH: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today said the government's proposal to abolish the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (AUKU) will be tabled at the Cabinet meeting this Wednesday.
"I will bring this to the Cabinet this Wednesday," the PKR president said after delivering his policy speech at the 2026 PKR National Congress at the Melaka International Trade Centre (MITC) here.
Earlier in his speech, Anwar announced the government would abolish the Act as part of its broader reform agenda, particularly in response to concerns raised by university students.
He said several amendments had already been made to give students greater freedom, but acknowledged that some remained dissatisfied and had submitted a memorandum calling for further changes.
Anwar said the abolition was among several reforms the government intended to pursue more decisively after initially prioritising political stability, national security and economic growth.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Tabung Haji RCI: Shipping CEO, directors among seven held by MACC
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A shipping company chief executive officer with a Datuk title is among seven people detained by the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) to assist investigations into the Tabung Haji (TH) Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI).
Also detained were a company director and a former company director, both holding Datuk and Datuk Seri titles respectively, as well as four former senior TH management officers.
Sources said all seven suspects were detained in stages between 3pm and 10.30pm yesterday at the MACC headquarters in Putrajaya.
The first suspect, a shipping company CEO in his 60s with the title of Datuk, was arrested for allegedly submitting documents containing false details in payments to TH, involving the falsification of a petroleum company's contract for his company's benefit.
The second and third suspects, both in their 60s and holding Datuk and Datuk Seri titles respectively, were detained for allegedly deceiving TH officers into investing in a construction company by promising a potential listing on Bursa Malaysia.
The four former senior TH management officers, aged between their 50s and 60s, including a Datuk Seri and a woman, were detained over alleged involvement in corrupt practices.
Their actions allegedly led TH to enter into a RM2.72 billion lease agreement with a Saudi Arabian company for four hotels, resulting in financial losses to the pilgrimage fund.
Only two male suspects — the shipping company CEO and a construction company director with a Datuk title — were remanded.
The remaining five were released on MACC bail due to health issues.
Magistrate Ahmad Afiq Hasan issued a five-day remand order, until Aug 19, against the two suspects at the Putrajaya magistrate's court today.
Sources said the arrests followed investigations by a special task force set up by MACC to review the TH RCI report, which was published on the Department of Islamic Development Malaysia (Jakim) portal on July 29.
When contacted, MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman confirmed the arrests, saying the case was being investigated under Sections 18 and 16(a)(A) of the MACC Act 2009.
The TH RCI report, released on July 29, identified various management and governance weaknesses at the institution between 2014 and 2020 and made 25 recommendations for improvement.
A special sitting of the Dewan Rakyat was held last Tuesday to table and debate the report.

Title: South Korean AI chip tycoon appeals record US$666m divorce ruling
Article:
SEOUL: South Korea's AI chip tycoon has appealed a court ruling ordering him to pay US$666 million to his former wife in the country's largest-ever divorce settlement, his lawyers said Saturday.
Chey Tae-won, 65, is the chairman of the SK Group, which owns world-leading memory chipmaker SK hynix – a pillar of South Korea's tech-led economy.
Seoul High Court in 2024 had told him to pay 1.38 trillion won to his ex-wife Roh Soh-yeong, and the sum – equal to more than US$1 billion at the exchange rate at the time of the ruling – led local media to dub it the "divorce of the century."
Chey appealed to the Supreme Court, which told the high court to reconsider its 2024 decision and led to the tycoon's reduced divorce bill of 944 billion won (US$666 million) in July this year – still the largest divorce asset settlement ever awarded in South Korea.
Seoul High Court ruled last month that Roh was entitled to a cash payout worth one-third of the couple's marital assets, including Chey's SK shares, citing her family role and support for SK Group activities.
The tycoon has appealed that July ruling, his lawyers said Saturday, which brings the case to the country's highest court again.
"After careful consideration of various factors, Chairman Chey Tae-won has filed an appeal to the Supreme Court," his lawyers said in a statement sent to AFP.
"We will approach the upcoming procedures with a commitment to minimising any negative impact on shareholders and the Group's management."
Roh's legal team declined to comment to AFP.
The appeal could extend a closely watched legal battle that has drawn attention to Chey's control of SK Group as the AI boom boosts the value of its chip assets.
SK Group shares have more than tripled in value since December 2015, when Chey publicly disclosed his extramarital affair.
South Korean outlet Money Today reported that Chey offered Roh a mix of stock and cash to settle the asset division to limit market impact, but she reportedly demanded full payment in cash, which would require him to sell a large amount of shares – prompting his appeal.
Chey and Roh – daughter of a former South Korea president – married in 1988 and have three children together, but the couple are believed to have lived apart for more than 15 years. In 2015 Chey admitted to fathering a child with his lover.
The 2024 ruling ordering the payout to Roh cited a 30 billion won slush fund her ex-president father, Roh Tae-woo, used to propel SK Group's growth.
But in October the Supreme Court quashed that argument, saying that any such cash likely stemmed from illegal bribes and therefore should not be counted.
The Supreme Court had separately ordered Chey and his lover to pay Roh 2 billion won in alimony, which his lover, Kim Hee-young, paid in 2024.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar denies rift with Zahid, says ties remain good
Article:
AYER KEROH: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today dismissed claims of a strained relationship with Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, saying ties between them remained good at the national level.
Anwar, who is also PKR president, described former Umno Youth chief Khairy Jamaluddin's assessment of his relationship with the Umno president as a personal view shaped by a tendency to view politics through conflict.
"That is his personal view. He always looks at things from the perspective of conflict.
"I see things differently. He is on the path of conflict, I am on the path of peace," he told reporters after his policy speech at the 2026 PKR National Congress at the Melaka International Trade Centre (MITC) here.
Anwar said he had specifically thanked Zahid and Umno in his speech for their role in strengthening cooperation within the unity government.
Asked whether his relationship with Zahid remained good at the national level, Anwar replied: "Still good."
He, however, acknowledged that there were some disagreements between the parties at the state level.
"At the state level, there is a little. That is normal," he said.
Yesterday, Khairy claimed that trust between Anwar and Zahid was now at its lowest point since the unity government was formed in 2022.
He attributed this to increasingly strained ties between Barisan Nasional and Pakatan Harapan, particularly following BN's decision to cooperate with Perikatan Nasional in the Negri Sembilan state election.
Khairy said the cooperation had created a major rift between BN and PH, raising questions over how far BN would continue to support the unity government.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Teacher in student, mother assault probe released on police bail
Article:
PASIR MAS: A 54-year-old teacher remanded over the alleged assault of a 14-year-old student and his mother was released on police bail this morning.
District police chief Assistant Commissioner Mazlan Hassan said the suspect was released after his three-day remand order expired today.
"The suspect was released on police bail this morning after his remand ended today," he said when contacted.
The teacher was arrested on Wednesday after the student's 42-year-old mother lodged a police report over the alleged incident.
In her report, the woman claimed her son was assaulted at a secondary school on Aug 11, where he was allegedly struck on the head with a cane.
The woman said she went to meet the teacher the following day to discuss the incident and alleged that the teacher hit her with a cane on her right thigh.
Following the report, police obtained a
three-day remand
order against the teacher from Aug 13 to Aug 15.
The case is being investigated under Section 324 of the Penal Code for voluntarily causing hurt by means of a weapon or other dangerous means.

Title: UK slams Netanyahu over 'Islamic republic of Britain' remark
Article:
JERUSALEM: Britain on Friday hit back at Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu derisively calling the country an "Islamic republic" in an interview, branding the remarks "completely unacceptable."
The diplomatic tit-for-tat came after the right-wing prime minister made the reference in an army radio podcast interview the previous day, in which he criticised the UK's stance on Israel.
It echoed the language of far-right politicians and commentators in the Western world who have made baseless claims that parts of Britain have come under Islamic law due to immigration, drawing accusations of Islamophobia.
"These comments are completely unacceptable and we have raised them with the Israeli Government," a UK government spokesman said Friday.
In the podcast interview, Netanyahu spoke of how Winston Churchill's grandson and namesake vocally supported Israel during the 1967 Arab-Israeli war.
"Would you find that now?" Netanyahu asked.
"Someone once said that the first Islamic republic with nuclear weapons would be the Islamic republic of Britain," he added with a smile. "We're making sure there's not another one here in Iran."
In a BBC radio interview earlier Friday, Israeli government spokesman David Mencer appeared to downplay Netanyahu's comments.
"He [Netanyahu] was making a quote that someone else had given," Mencer said, noting United States Vice President JD Vance had "made those comments" previously.
"He was quoting what the vice president had said."
Vance told the Munich Security Summit in 2024 that the UK could become "the first truly Islamist country that will get a nuclear weapon", drawing a rebuke from senior UK politicians at the time.
Britain was one of a number of European countries that recognised Palestinian statehood last year, infuriating Israel.
More recently, its new prime minister Andy Burnham has said that his predecessor Keir Starmer did not put enough pressure on Israel to halt its offensive in Gaza.
In an interview with The Guardian shortly before taking office, Burnham said that Britain would consider banning trade in goods from Israeli settlements in the West Bank, which Israel has occupied since 1967.
Britain, usually closely aligned with Washington, has also kept its distance from the US-Israeli war launched in February against Iran.
Netanyahu has long vowed to prevent Iran from acquiring nuclear weapons, a goal that Teheran denies pursuing.
Britain and the US are nuclear powers, and Israel is widely known to have atomic weapons, although it has never publicly acknowledged its arsenal.
In 1998, Pakistan became the first Islamic nuclear power when it tested an atom bomb in response to parallel tests by its historic rival India.--aFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka MRSM Alor Gajah students sought treatment before being found at Central Market
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The two 16-year-old MRSM Alor Gajah students who were reported missing had sought treatment at a nearby health clinic before they were found at Central Market last night.
City police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said the pair were found by Alor Gajah district police personnel about 10.30pm.
"Before being found, both of them had sought treatment at a nearby health clinic after reportedly feeling unwell.
"They were then taken to Kuala Lumpur Hospital (HKL) for further medical examinations before being handed over to their families," he said in a statement.
Fadil said police are still investigating the circumstances surrounding the incident.
The two students, Siti Nur Aaira Aidi and Nur Aisy Humaira Mohd Saad, had been reported missing since Tuesday.
Earlier, Majlis Amanah Rakyat (Mara) chairman Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki confirmed that the students were found at
Central Market
at 10.31pm yesterday.
"Alhamdulillah, police found both Siti Nur Aaira and Nur Aisy Humaira," he said in a Facebook post.
Police had earlier sought public assistance to trace the teenagers after a teacher lodged a report on Tuesday.

Title: 19 million US eggs recalled over deadly Salmonella risk
Article:
WASHINGTON: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has said some 19 million eggs that were voluntarily recalled pose a reasonable risk of serious health consequences, including death.
Midwest Poultry Services voluntarily recalled the eggs over potential contamination with Salmonella Enteritidis on July 22.
The bacteria is linked to sometimes fatal infections, especially in young children, the elderly and people with weakened immunity.
On Wednesday, the FDA designated the recall category as Class 1, meaning "a situation in which there is a reasonable probability that the use of or exposure to a violative product will cause serious adverse health consequences or death."
The eggs were produced in Texas between June 6 and July 3, 2026, with sell by or best by dates between July 20 and Aug 17, 2026. They were distributed to stores and retail consumers in Texas, Oklahoma, Arkansas, Louisiana, New Mexico, and Mississippi.
In all, 1,589,577 dozen eggs were covered by the recall, and included both white shell eggs and brown cage free shell eggs under a variety of brand names.
The company said it "identified the issue on two of its farm locations in Texas through proactive environmental monitoring practices and a robust internal investigation. The company also initiated its own testing protocols to identify potential sources of" salmonella.
"Do not consume the eggs. You should throw your eggs away or return them to your retailer for a full refund."
It added it was not aware of any specific illnesses linked to its products.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Rohingya father, two young sons die in Bagan Serai house fire
Article:
BAGAN SERAI: A father and his two young sons were found burnt to death in a room after a fire broke out at their home in Taman Serai Maju here early today.
The victims, all Rohingya nationals, were identified as Mohd Yunus Nor Ali, 27, and his sons Muhammad Woheed Mohd Yunus, six, and Mohamad Aheed Mohd Yunus, three.
His wife, Saniya Jahan Juma Abul Kasim, 24, suffered burns to her hands and feet and was taken to hospital for treatment.
Perak Fire and Rescue Department director Datuk Sayani Saidon said the department received an emergency call at 5.17am before firefighters were dispatched to the scene.
He said two fire engines and an Emergency Medical Rescue Services (EMRS) vehicle arrived at the house at 5.30am.
"Upon arrival, firefighters found a Class A house, about 70 per cent engulfed in flames.
"A woman was found outside the house suffering burns to her hands and feet. She told firefighters that her husband and two sons were trapped inside," she said.
She said firefighters immediately launched a search and rescue operation and found the three victims inside an empty room that was on fire.
Sayani said the firefighters used a 100-foot hose line and a booster line supplied with water from the fire engine's tank and a nearby drain to extinguish the blaze.
"The fire was brought under control at 6.20am and the operation ended at 7.35am.
"The three victims were pronounced dead at the scene by Health Ministry personnel before their bodies were handed over to the police for further action," she said.
Sayani said a thorough investigation is being conducted at the scene to determine the exact cause of the fire and estimate the losses.
"Based on preliminary information and findings by the department's Fire Forensics Unit, the fire is believed to have started in the first room, where the victims were found.
"The cause of the fire and the total losses are still under investigation," she said.
She added that 24 firefighters and six members of the volunteer fire brigade were also involved in the operation, along with seven policemen and three Health Ministry personnel.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar announces abolition of Universities and University Colleges Act
Article:
AYER KEROH: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today announced that his government would abolish the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (Act 30).
The PKR president said that although several amendments had previously been made, some matters remained unsatisfactory to university students.
"University students feel that they should be free. We have freed them through amendments to AUKU, but there are still those who are dissatisfied, and they have submitted a memorandum.
"Therefore, today I want to announce that we will abolish the Universities and University Colleges Act," he said when delivering the PKR president's policy speech at the 2026 Keadilan National Congress at the Melaka International Trade Centre here today according to Berita Harian.
Also present were PKR and Unity Government leaders, including PKR deputy president Nurul Izzah Anwar, Gabungan Rakyat Sabah chairman Datuk Seri Hajiji Nor and Parti Amanah Negara president Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu.
AUKU has been amended seven times since it was introduced in 1971, with the 2012 amendment allowing university students to participate in activities organised by political parties outside campus.
AUKU was also amended in 1971, 1975, 1983, 1996 and 2009.
The latest amendment in 2024 saw disciplinary action against students at public universities no longer fall under the authority of vice-chancellors, but instead be decided by the Student Disciplinary Committee through an amendment to Section 16B of AUKU.
In addition, the amendment saw improvements to Section 15A of AUKU, allowing Student Representative Councils  and student bodies to collect money and receive contributions in any manner, subject to the regulations and written laws in force.
Meanwhile, Anwar said several education reforms had already been successfully implemented by his administration.
"What we have done is to organise the admission of our children at the early education level, provide TVET and STEM materials in a more structured manner, and take over preschool education for all our children.
"We do not want preschool education to be only for the elite in urban areas and second-class for children in the interior and rural areas. Therefore, this has become the responsibility of the Ministry of Education," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: TNB targets 40,000 mangrove saplings nationwide
Article:
NIBONG TEBAL: Tenaga Nasional Berhad's (TNB) My Brighter Green Initiative (MBGI) 2026 planted 1,500 mangrove saplings at the Chenaam Fishermen's Jetty in Sungai Acheh to restore coastal ecosystems and help protect fisheries resources.
The planting was carried out in collaboration with the Malaysian Nature Society (MNS), bringing the total number of trees planted to date to 39,000.
TNB Chief Retail Officer Datuk Kamal Arifin A. Rahman said mangrove planting was important in coastal areas as the trees served as breeding grounds for marine life while helping to reduce coastal erosion.
"As the country's leading energy utility, TNB believes economic development and electricity supply security must go hand in hand with environmental responsibility.
"Based on this principle, TNB continues to strengthen its Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) agenda through various initiatives that support the Net Zero 2050 aspiration," he said in his speech at the MBGI 2026 programme at the Chenaam Fishermen's Jetty in Sungai Acheh here today, the fifth location for the programme.
Kamal Arifin said TNB was targeting the planting of 40,000 mangrove saplings at six locations nationwide under MBGI 2026, which was estimated to absorb about 680 tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent (tCO₂e) per annum, comparable to removing the carbon emissions of 159 petrol-powered passenger vehicles each year.
He said the greening effort continued TNB's initiative which, since 2017, had seen nearly 200,000 trees planted nationwide, with an estimated absorption of about 3,140 tCO₂e annually.
He said the selection of the Chenaam Fishermen's Jetty as one of the programme's locations was particularly significant given its location in an estuary and coastal area rich in mangrove forest ecosystems, which were also gazetted as a forest reserve and closely linked to the livelihoods of the fishing community.
"These mangrove forests serve as breeding grounds for fish, prawns and crabs, besides acting as a natural barrier to reduce coastal erosion and enhance the resilience of coastal areas to climate change," he said.
The event was officiated by Penang Rural Development, Agro-technology and Food Security, and Entrepreneurship Committee chairman Datuk Rashidi Zinol, who is also Sungai Acheh assemblyman.
Rashidi said the selection of the Chenaam Fishermen's Jetty as the MBGI 2026 location provided added value to the coastal community as mangrove conservation was closely linked to the sustainability of fisheries resources and the wellbeing of local fishermen.
He said the effort was not merely about planting mangrove saplings, but also involved conserving coastal ecosystems, protecting biodiversity and ensuring that the sources of livelihood of the fishing community could be sustained for future generations.
"Thank you to TNB for choosing Sungai Acheh and Sungai Chenaam as the location for this year's MBGI mangrove planting project. This area remains a treasure and will certainly benefit the residents, especially fishermen in the surrounding areas," he said.
At the event, TNB also presented RM67,500 in corporate social responsibility (CSR) contributions to TVET MARA Seberang Perai Utara, Nibong Tebal Vocational College, SK Sungai Setar, SMK Taman Widuri, SMK Methodist Nibong Tebal, as well as the Sungai Acheh Fishermen's Association and community.
Kamal Arifin said that from 2025 to June 2026, TNB had channelled RM2.8 million through various CSR and wakalah initiatives for the benefit of communities in Penang, while RM31.6 million was allocated nationwide during the first six months of 2026 for various CSR programmes benefiting people across the country.
Meanwhile, food basket recipient Siti Meriam Abdul Hamid, 71, said the contribution was meaningful as it helped ease her family's expenses, particularly as she had two sons with disabilities, aged 42 and 44.
"The other residents and I who received food basket assistance today greatly appreciate TNB's concern and continued attention to the needs of the local community, and we hope this can continue in the future," she said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nine areas in Sarawak record unhealthy API readings as Sibu joins list
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Sibu became the latest area in Sarawak to record an unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) reading, bringing the total number of locations in that category to nine as of 9am today.
Data from the Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal showed Kuching recorded the highest reading at 167, followed by Samarahan (164), Serian (163), Sarikei (157), Bintulu (156), Sri Aman (154), Mukah (152), Sibu (131), and Samalaju (126).
Meanwhile, 46 areas nationwide recorded moderate API readings, while 13 areas recorded good air quality.
API readings between zero and 50 denote good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy, and above 300 hazardous.
Hourly API data is updated from 68 air quality monitoring stations across the nation.

Title: [UPDATED] Anwar to PKR leaders: Being in power does not mean you are the best
Article:
AYER KEROH:  PKR president Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim reminded party leaders today that holding government positions did not make them superior to others, urging them to return to the ground and listen to the people's grievances.
"We cannot connect effectively with our masses. We need to do this. How do we do this?
"You are ministers; that does not necessarily mean you are the best. You're deputy ministers; you hold all these positions; this is a challenge. Listen, make the necessary adjustments and be prepared to change," he said in his policy speech at the 2026 PKR National Congress at the Melaka International Trade Centre here.
Anwar, who is prime minister, said leaders must listen with a willingness to change rather than merely preparing to respond or argue, as PKR sought to reconnect with voters despite the government's achievements.
"Do not listen in order to respond and lecture," he said, adding that party leaders had to understand the concerns and frustrations expressed by ordinary Malaysians.
Anwar acknowledged that while the government had recorded encouraging economic performance and gained international recognition, those achievements had not necessarily translated into public support.
He said PKR itself had to accept responsibility for weaknesses in communicating the government's achievements and understanding the concerns raised by voters, rather than looking elsewhere for explanations.
Anwar urged party leaders to practise accountability and resist the temptation to attribute declining support to racial, regional or other factors, saying the party instead had to examine its own shortcomings.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Fallen trees require systematic prevention, says Fire Dept
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Fallen trees are a growing public safety concern, with the Fire and Rescue Department calling for regular safety audits, better data sharing and consistent maintenance to prevent deaths and injuries.
Director-general Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohammad said 26,001 fallen-tree incidents were recorded nationwide from 2021 to June 2026, resulting in 50 deaths and 243 injuries.
He said emergency calls involving fallen trees remained high, at between 4,400 and 5,200 cases annually, with 1,912 incidents recorded in the first six months of this year alone.
A total of 360 people were rescued unhurt during the period.
"Although the number of cases has not consistently increased, fallen trees continue to pose a serious risk to public safety," he said.
Recent incidents have highlighted the danger.
On Aug 3, the Maran Umno Youth chief was among four people killed when a tree fell onto Jalan Lama Bentong near the Janda Baik entrance in Bentong.
On July 19, a 43-year-old man died after a fallen tree near the Singapore Embassy on Jalan Tun Razak, Kuala Lumpur, crushed his car.
Nor Hisham said thunderstorms with strong winds and heavy rain, particularly during monsoon transitions, were among the main factors contributing to fallen trees.
Prolonged rain could saturate the soil and weaken root systems, increasing the risk of trees toppling, he said.
Other contributing factors included age, disease, decay and weak root or branch structures.
A recent Penang Island City Council investigation found that a 90-year-old angsana tree that fell on Jalan Macalister on Aug 3 had rotting roots, cavities at the base of the trunk, chronic soil compaction, and limited root space.
Nor Hisham said the department viewed fallen trees as the result of multiple factors involving weather, tree condition and maintenance.
He said local authorities, premises owners and relevant agencies should conduct regular safety audits, particularly along main roads and around schools, hospitals, public parks, residential areas and other high-footfall locations.
The audits should be carried out with qualified experts and cover tree trunks, branches, canopies and root systems, as well as signs of leaning, decay, disease and the impact of surrounding development.
"High-risk trees require immediate action, including pruning, treatment, structural support or controlled felling.
"Regular audits allow early signs of structural failure to be identified before an incident occurs, reducing risks to lives, property and public pathways," he said.
While tree management falls under the respective authorities, Nor Hisham said the department was ready to share incident data, map high-risk areas and coordinate weather preparedness.
He urged local authorities to make full use of its data on fallen trees to identify recurring hotspots, while suggesting joint inspections, pre-monsoon coordination and faster reporting channels.
On operational readiness, Nor Hisham said the department had sufficient personnel, machinery and equipment to respond to routine and localised incidents.
The department also works with local authorities, police, the Civil Defence Force, utility companies, the Public Works Department and other agencies to clear fallen trees, manage traffic and secure affected areas.
He advised the public to monitor weather forecasts issued by MetMalaysia through its official website, the myCuaca application and official social media channels.--BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Anwar: Government to step up reform agenda
Article:
AYER KEROH: PKR president Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the government would pursue its reform agenda more aggressively.
Anwar, who is also Prime Minister, said the government had initially prioritised political stability, national security and economic growth, but believed sufficient progress had been achieved in those areas to allow the administration to move more decisively on reforms.
"Political stability has been achieved, national security is assured and the economy is growing strongly. Now, we will press ahead more firmly with the reform agenda," he said in his policy speech at the 2026 PKR National Congress at the Melaka International Trade Centre (MITC) here.
Anwar said several reform measures had already been implemented under his administration, although others would require more time.
Anwar said the political cooperation that led to the formation of the Unity Government following the 15th General Election in 2022 also required Pakatan Harapan (PH) to negotiate with its coalition partners in pursuing its reform agenda.
"Those who are calling for change, please do so. But accept the fact that changes have already been made. We can list many of them.
"What does the courage of Madani reform mean? These are things that should have been done over the previous 60 years, but were not.
"So, even if we criticise, urge and demand more, do not erase the fact that reforms have already been carried out," he said.
Anwar cited several measures implemented under his administration, including amendments to the Audit Act 1957, the Parliamentary Services Act and the Public Finance and Fiscal Responsibility Act 2023, the establishment of the Special Task Force on Agency Reform, as well as the Consumer Credit Act 2025 and Gig Workers Act 2025.
He said he had remained consistent in pursuing the reform agenda championed by PH since returning to federal power in 2022.
"There were those who assumed at the time that we could change everything at once. I want to remind them that sometimes, even our colleagues in the cabinet were not as bold as they were when they were outside the government.
"We know that change must take root and be carried out in stages. This is not an excuse to avoid reform. We have also learnt, and I have always reminded everyone not to rush, as I have said at several PKR meetings and congresses," he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] PKR Congress: There was indeed 'sakau' involving Tabung Haji, says Anwar
Article:
AYER KEROH:  PKR president Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today said there had been "sakau" (embezzlement) involving Tabung Haji, as detailed in the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) into the institution.
Anwar, who is prime minister, said the pilgrimage fund had suffered RM12 billion in losses.
"People do not like the term 'sakau'. I want to repeat it here in Melaka: there was indeed 'sakau' involving Tabung Haji. RM12 billion was lost, not embezzlement? There is (embezzlement)," he said in his policy speech at the 2026 PKR National Congress at the Melaka International Trade Centre here today.
Anwar said His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, had told him that action against corruption should not stop with Tabung Haji, but should also extend to other agencies, including Felda.
He said he had ordered enforcement agencies to act firmly against anyone found to have violated regulations or misappropriated assets entrusted to them, regardless of political affiliation, position or race.
"Do not delay, do not compromise. It does not matter which party, what position or what race. If they are guilty, if they are 'penyakau', arrest them," he said.
He stressed, however, that investigations must be carried out professionally and that no one should be prejudged before the authorities completed their investigations.
Anwar said that while only a small number of individuals may have been responsible for the alleged wrongdoing, the financial consequences were ultimately borne by Malaysians as a whole.
"Those who embezzled were only a few, but the ones who have to pay are all Malaysians — Malays, Chinese, Indians, Ibans, Kadazans — because of their greed and deception," he said.
Anwar said the RCI report had been completed before he became prime minister, adding that he nevertheless accepted responsibility for it not being disclosed earlier.
He said the eventual decision to disclose the report was made by the cabinet, despite concerns over the possible impact of making its findings public.
Anwar said the government was open to suggestions for the RCI's scope to be extended to cover Tabung Haji's operations after 2020.
"Some have suggested that we should not stop after 2020, but continue, and I said, yes, continue," he said.
He also took a swipe at opposition MPs who walked out of a special Dewan Rakyat sitting convened to debate the RCI findings.
"We disclosed it, but there were those who were afraid to debate it openly and ran away from Parliament," he added.

Title: Two dead after powerful 7.7-magnitude quake hits Indonesia
Article:
JAKARTAL  At least two people died after an earthquake of magnitude 7.7 and dozens of aftershocks struck off eastern Indonesia early on Saturday, the authorities said.
Tsunami waves of less than 1 metre were recorded in several areas of the Southeast Asian nation. The tsunami warning was lifted about three hours after the quake.
In addition to the deaths of at least two, one person was injured in Sikka Regency, the disaster mitigation agency BNPB said in a statement.
Parts of a building collapsed into dust and rubble as people screamed and ran in the street, a video on Facebook, verified by Reuters as being at a port in Maumere, showed. It is the main town in Sikka Regency on Flores Island in the east of Indonesia's vast archipelago.
Strong shaking was felt across East Nusa Tenggara, West Nusa Tenggara and parts of South Sulawesi, and residents in several areas reported shaking lasting about one minute, BNPB said.
"Most of the people felt the shock and scattered out of their homes," it said.
A hospital in the district of Ende in East Nusa Tenggara Province was moving patients outside, Kompas TV footage showed, and Kompas.com reported at least one landslide.
Geophysics agency BMKG recorded the first quake at 4.58am (2158 GMT) at a depth of 15km, followed by several aftershocks.
Australia's tsunami warning centre said the undersea earthquake would have "no tsunami threat to the Australian mainland, islands or territories". - REUTERS PIC
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: From 'normal guy' to killer: Mangione's anger at US insurers
Article:
WASHINGTON: The man who admitted to shooting dead a US health insurance executive used a charged courtroom appearance to blame a back injury for his crimes that he said sought to make "health care work better for everyone."
Luigi Mangione, 28, was thrust into the spotlight in 2024 after gunning down UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson, a father of two, in broad daylight in Manhattan.
The case laid bare deep frustration and anger with America's privatised medical system that Mangione said failed him after a back injury.
Speculation about Mangione's motives exploded after his dramatic capture in Pennsylvania after a tipster spotted him at a McDonald's.
Mangione has amassed an army of ardent fans and followers who lavish him with prison mail and donations to his defense fund.
His critics, led by US President Donald Trump, have called for him to face severe punishment.
A photo on one of his social media accounts included an X-ray of an apparently injured spine.
While no explicit political affiliation has emerged, an apparent manifesto found on Mangione after his arrest contained anti-corporate sentiments.
It targeted the health insurance industry, referring to it as a "greed-fuelled cartel" that "extracts human life force for money."
According to Mangione's LinkedIn profile, he had been employed as a data engineer at TrueCar, a California-based online auto marketplace, a role he left in 2023.
Although he had been living in Hawaii ahead of the killing, he originally hails from Towson, Maryland, near Baltimore. He comes from a prominent and wealthy Italian-American family.
The family owns local businesses, including the Hayfields Country Club.
- 'COWARDS AND PREDATORS' -
A gifted student, Mangione graduated at the top of his high school class in 2016. In an interview with his local paper at the time, he praised his teachers for fostering a passion for learning beyond grades and encouraging intellectual curiosity.
A former student who knew Mangione at the Gilman School told AFP the suspect struck him as "a normal guy, nice kid."
"There was nothing about him that was off, at least from my perception," they said, asking that their name not be used.
"Seemed to just be smiling, and kind of seemed like he was a smart kid. Ended up being valedictorian, which confirmed that," the former student said.
Mangione went on to attend the prestigious University of Pennsylvania, where he completed both a bachelor's and master's degree in computer science by 2020, according to a university spokesperson.
While at Penn, Mangione helped lead a group of 60 undergraduates who collaborated on video game projects, according to online archives.
On Instagram, Mangione shared snapshots of his travels in Mexico, Puerto Rico and Hawaii. He also posted shirtless photos flaunting a six-pack and appeared in celebratory posts with fellow members of the Phi Kappa Psi fraternity.
However, it is on X (formerly Twitter) that users have scoured Mangione's posts for potential motives. His header photo showed an X-ray of a spine with bolts.
Finding a coherent political ideology has also proved elusive, though he had written a review of Ted Kaczynski's manifesto on the online site Goodreads, calling it "prescient."
Kaczynski, known as the Unabomber, carried out a string of bombings in the United States from 1978 to 1995, a campaign he said was aimed at halting the advance of modern society and technology.
Mangione called Kaczynski "rightfully imprisoned," while also saying "'violence never solved anything' is a statement uttered by cowards and predators."
Mangione has also linked approvingly to posts criticising secularism as a harmful consequence of Christianity's decline.
He previously wrote, "Horror vacui (nature abhors a vacuum)." He subsequently posted an essay he wrote in high school titled "How Christianity Prospered by Appealing to the Lower Classes of Ancient Rome."
Mangione, who reportedly acts as something of an "ambassador" to new arrivals in his cell block, now faces life imprisonment for his crimes at sentencing in December.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 7.7-magnitude quake sparks mass evacuation in Indonesia, tsunami warning lifted
Article:
MAUMERE, Indonesia: A strong 7.7-magnitude earthquake struck off Flores island in eastern Indonesia early Saturday, sending thousands running in panic after authorities issued a tsunami warning.
Residents in Nagekeo regency, the area closest to the epicentre, raced for higher ground as the sea retreated – a possible sign of an approaching tsunami, AFP journalists saw.
The warning was later lifted.
The epicentre of the shallow quake was located off the north coast of the island, about 68km northwest of the coastal town of Ende, US and Indonesian authorities said.
The initial jolt was followed by strong aftershocks in the same area, including one with a magnitude of 6.1.
"Suddenly it started to shake and I panicked," 31-year-old hospital customer service official and Maumre resident, Lukas Lotar, told AFP.
"Patients also fled the hospital, the jolt was big. I saw some walls were cracked," he said.
A resident in Nagekeo, Yohanes Babo, 56, said he was at a market when the earth started shaking.
"The shaking was strong. Thankfully, we were already outside the house," he told AFP.
"People were panicking, running here and there. We're evacuating for the time being... and trying to get to the hills," he said, adding: "My family is safe. No one was harmed."
- EVACUATION URGED -
Indonesia's Meteorology, Climatology, and Geophysics Agency (BMKG) warned of the possibility of tsunami waves following the quake and urged people to get to higher ground.
"We strongly urge our communities along the northern coast of Flores and in the southern parts, on the southern islands and across the southern region, to carry out self-evacuation immediately," Abdul Muhari, an official at the national disaster agency, BNPB, said.
Residents should "move away from the shore, either by going more than two kilometres inland or by moving up into hilly areas more than 10 meters high," he told local broadcaster Kompas TV.
BMKG earthquake and tsunami director Wijayanto said tsunami modelling suggested the potential for a tsunami in the provinces of East Nusa Tenggara, South Sulawesi, and West Nusa Tenggara.
An alert was issued for waves ranging from 0.5 metres to three metres, but was later lifted.
"We have ended (the tsunami warning) but we will keep monitoring the sea level," said Wijayanto, who like many Indonesians, goes by one name.
Residents in the town of Maumere on Flores Island were evacuating to higher ground, an AFP correspondent saw.
Images broadcast on Indonesian television showed hundreds of people in nearby Nagekeo regency evacuating the area from among the rubble of damaged buildings.
Authorities have not reported any casualties, but said tsunami waves between 19 and 30cm have been detected.
Indonesia and neighbouring countries experience frequent earthquakes due to their location in the Pacific "Ring of Fire" – an arc of intense seismic activity stretching from Japan through Southeast Asia and across the Pacific basin.
Among Indonesia's history of deadly quakes is a devastating 9.1-magnitude tremor in 2004 that struck off the coast of Sumatra and triggered a tsunami that killed 220,000 throughout the region, including about 170,000 in Indonesia.
The Boxing Day tragedy was one of the deadliest natural disasters in recorded history.
In 2018, a powerful quake shook the island of Lombok and several more tremors followed over the next couple of weeks, killing more than 550 people on the holiday island and neighbouring Sumbawa.
Later that year, a 7.5-magnitude quake and a subsequent tsunami in Palu on Sulawesi island left more than 4,300 people dead or missing.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Teenager killed, two injured in Kota Tinggi motorcycle crash
Article:
KOTA TINGGI: A 15-year-old boy was killed, while two others sustained injuries in a two-motorcycle crash at the Taman Anggerik junction here last night.
District police chief Superintendent Yusof Othman said police received a report on the incident involving a Yamaha Ego Scooter and a Kawasaki KR150 motorcycle at 9.05pm.
He said the victim, who was riding pillion on the scooter, suffered serious head and body injuries and was pronounced dead at the scene by an assistant medical officer.
"The two motorcyclists, aged 15 and 26, sustained injuries and are receiving treatment at Kluang Hospital," he said in a statement today.
He said the body had been taken to the Kota Tinggi Hospital Forensic Unit for the necessary procedures and the case was being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
"Members of the public with information on the accident are urged to come forward and contact the traffic division of the district police headquarters to assist in the investigation," he said.

Title: 3 family members killed in Pahang house fire [WATCH]
Article:
KUANTAN: Three family members were killed in a house fire in Desa Mawar, Muadzam Shah, Rompin, early this morning.
Pahang Fire and Rescue Department Operations Division assistant director Mohd Salahuddin Isa said an emergency call was received at 4.11am and a team of firefighters was deployed to the scene.
He said the fire claimed the lives of a man, his wife and their son, while two other children survived.
The blaze destroyed the family's home, while a neighbouring house was about 70 per cent damaged. All six occupants escaped unharmed.
The cause of the fire and the total value of the losses are still under investigation.

Title: Fuziah says PKR must rebuild after electoral setbacks
Article:
AYER KEROH: PKR secretary-general Datuk Dr Fuziah Salleh said the party is entering its national congress wounded by recent electoral setbacks and shifts in political alliances, but its struggle is far from over.
She said the party was not gathering at a time when morale was at its highest, after a difficult period that had left a significant impact on its members.
"We come to this congress wounded and hurt. We are not here when our spirits are at their peak," she said in her welcoming address at the 2026 PKR national congress at the Melaka International Trade Centre here today.
Fuziah said several elections had tested PKR's strength, with the party losing political ground in areas it had previously regarded as strongholds, including states it once governed.
She said PKR had also experienced changes in political relationships that were difficult for members to accept, including former allies taking directions the party had not expected.
"There were those who once travelled with us who have now chosen a path we could hardly believe they would take.
"It is like sharing the same pillow but having different dreams. It has left us hurt," she said.
However, Fuziah said the congress should not become a platform to point fingers, assign blame or seek retaliation over what had happened.
Instead, she urged members to honestly examine the party's weaknesses, learn from its setbacks and focus on rebuilding its strength.
"We cannot pretend that nothing happened. We must acknowledge that we have been disappointed, saddened and hurt. But we cannot allow those wounds to determine our future," she said.
Fuziah reminded delegates that PKR had survived far more difficult periods, pointing to the 2004 general election when the party was reduced to just one parliamentary seat, Permatang Pauh, while party president Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim was still in prison.
She said the party nevertheless continued building its organisation, strengthening its membership and taking its reform message to the people, eventually recovering from what had appeared to be an existential defeat.
"We may have lost the battle, but we will win the war. We will rise. We will continue the struggle and, InsyaAllah, we will win," she said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Last embrace: Family mourns teacher killed in LPT2 crash [WATCH]
Article:
MARANG: "That day, he shook hands with us and hugged us tightly while repeatedly apologising. We thought nothing of it at the time, but now we realise it may have been a sign that he was going to leave us forever."
Those were the words of Mohd Zukri Yaacob, 55, the elder brother of Mohd Fahimi Yaacob, 41, who died in a crash at Km357 of the East Coast Highway 2 (LPT2) near Bukit Besi, Dungun, early yesterday.
Zukri, the seventh of 14 siblings, said the family was still struggling to come to terms with the loss of their youngest brother, whom they regarded as a source of guidance and someone always ready to help.
He said he received the tragic news at about 10.15am while working at the Kuala Berang Health Clinic, when police contacted him.
"At first, I was shocked because the police only asked whether I had a younger brother named Fahimi who rode a motorcycle.
"I still could not believe it, so I called his wife to confirm. When she told me Fahimi was riding to Kuala Lumpur, I immediately had a bad feeling and realised the accident victim was probably my brother," he said after the burial at the Kampung Jerong Surau Muslim Cemetery here last night.
The deceased's remains arrived from the Dungun Hospital Forensic Department at 7pm and were taken to the village mosque for prayers.
More than 500 people attended the funeral prayer at the mosque, located opposite the deceased's mother's home.
Fahimi was buried at 10.30pm, witnessed by two of his four children, Ariq Muhammad Rifqi, 11, and Aqif Darwish, eight, as well as relatives, friends and villagers.
Zukri said the family was particularly moved by Fahimi's unusual behaviour several days before the crash during a family thanksgiving and tahlil gathering.
"Usually, he would be the most active person organising family events because he was a teacher.
"But that day, he just sat at the back. We thought he was tired after organising a student camping programme.
"After the gathering, he shook hands with and hugged our mother and all his siblings, repeatedly apologising. Now, we feel it was like a final farewell," he said tearfully.
Zukri said Fahimi, the 13th of 14 siblings, was well loved by the family for his helpful nature and was often the person they turned to for advice and assistance.
"Whenever there was a family matter, he was among those who helped the most. His loss is deeply felt," he said.
He said Fahimi's four children had also lost their father, particularly four-year-old Nur Adra Delisha, who was very close to him.
"The eldest, Nur Adelia Qairina, is in Form One, while she and her two younger brothers appear to be coping. But the youngest has been crying constantly because she was very close to her father. She understands that her father is gone," he said.
Despite their grief, Zukri said the family accepted Fahimi's death as God's will.
"We accept it. Perhaps Allah loved him more, and there must be wisdom behind what happened," he said.
In the crash at 5.30am yesterday, Fahimi, a
teacher
at Hulu Terengganu Sixth Form College, died after his motorcycle caught fire following a collision with a lorry that had veered onto the road shoulder at Km357 of LPT2 near Bukit Besi.
He was travelling to Kuala Lumpur for work at the time.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PKR National Congress begins with Anwar set to outline party direction
Article:
AYER KEROH: PKR's 2026 National Congress begins here today, with party president Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim set to outline its strategic agenda and direction.
Held under the theme "Memugar Reformasi, Membina Madani" (Revitalising Reformasi, Building Madani), the two-day congress is expected to provide a platform for the party to strengthen its direction while reaffirming the reformasi principles that underpin PKR's struggle amid the evolving political landscape.
Anwar, who is the prime minister, is scheduled to officiate the congress.
The congress began yesterday with the conferences of the party's two main wings, Angkatan Muda Keadilan and Wanita PKR, which were officiated by deputy president Nurul Izzah Anwar.
About 2,500 delegates and at least 3,000 observers from across the country are expected to attend the congress.
The presence of diplomatic representatives from several major world powers, including the United States, China, Japan and Australia, as well as leaders of local political parties, adds further significance to the congress.
The debate sessions will focus on key issues affecting the people, particularly the economy, education and political stability, with 16 speakers representing the states and party wings.
Besides serving as a platform to strengthen unity within the leadership, the congress also aims to renew PKR's commitment to upholding integrity, advancing social justice and continuing to champion the interests of vulnerable groups.
The Bill Kayong Award, meanwhile, will be presented to five families in recognition of the sacrifices of members who served the party with dedication until the end of their lives.
The congress also features participation by several ministries and agencies, including the National Registration Department and Immigration Department, which will provide information and services to delegates and visitors.
The Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry's 'Karnival Rahmah Mega' is also being held in conjunction with the congress and is open to the public.
Anwar is scheduled to deliver his winding-up speech tomorrow before adjourning the congress. -- BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Johor eatery shut down after flies, eggs found in food
Article:
JOHOR BARU: The Johor Baru City Council (MBJB) ordered an eatery here to close yesterday following a health inspection that uncovered flies in soup, fly eggs on raw chicken, and multiple hygiene violations.
An MBJB spokesman said the council viewed food safety and cleanliness seriously after inspecting the premises, which scored only 65 per cent, or a Grade C, for cleanliness.
He said inspectors found flies in soup and fly eggs on raw chicken, posing a direct contamination risk to consumers.
Several food handlers had not received anti-typhoid vaccinations and lacked food handler certificates, he said.
He said the sink was not fitted with a grease trap, allowing food waste and wash water to flow directly into the public drain. The cooking area was covered in food waste and grease spills.
In the preparation area, food items were stored uncovered, mixed, and exposed to flies. Refrigerator conditions were unsanitary, with spilt food waste and disorganised storage.
Workers were found operating without proper caps, aprons, or footwear, while wearing accessories during food handling. The eatery was also found using polystyrene containers for food packaging.
The spokesman said the closure order was issued under By-law 49(1) of the MBJB Licensing of Trades, Businesses and Industries By-laws 2016.
He reminded all food establishment operators that hygiene went beyond fulfilling licensing requirements, as it was a fundamental duty to public health and safety.
MBJB will continue conducting routine inspections and enforcement actions to ensure all eateries across Johor Baru strictly comply with established health and hygiene standards, he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Foreign kidnappers and burglars, woman burnt among major crimes this week
Article:
KUALA LUMPU: The rescue of two kidnapped victims - a Singaporean and a China national - after a shootout in Alor Star this week, grabbed the headlines after the case generated major developments in the next few days.
Two of the kidnappers were shot dead and it was later revealed that this was not the syndicate's first case. They were
linked to two previous kidnapping
cases in Kuala Lumpur, bringing the gang's involvement to four cases.
Police carried out follow-up raids in Kedah, Penang and Kuala Lumpur, arresting another six suspects.
The
syndicate targeted foreigners
by using job offers and online friendships to lure potential victims. Once the victims were within reach of the syndicate, they were abducted and held while ransom demands were made.
This was an organised kidnapping network which operated across several states.
Here is a list of the other major crime cases which occurred this week:
* Police crippled a suspected burglary gang involving
five Chinese nationals
following two raids in Sri Petaling and Pudu, Kuala Lumpur on Aug 9.
The arrests were made after a break-in at a residence in Taman Desa Petaling on Aug 4.
In that case, the victim suffered losses estimated at about RM6,000, involving cash, jewellery and a branded sling bag.
Police found housebreaking tools, a vehicle and more than RM10,000 in cash from the suspects.
* Police in Sabah crippled a
syndicate believed to have cheated
victims of about RM600,000 through fortune-telling, traditional healing and ritual cleansing services.
Twelve people — 10 women and two men, including seven Chinese nationals — were arrested in raids across Kota Kinabalu, Penampang, Keningau and Kota Belud on Aug 8 and 9.
The syndicate allegedly offered traditional medicine, treatment for illnesses and rituals to remove bad luck. Victims would then be introduced to women claiming to be fortune-tellers or healers.
Victims were persuaded to surrender cash or jewellery for supposed prayers, incantations or cleansing rituals.
The valuables were then allegedly stolen or swapped with other objects placed inside bags, which victims were instructed not to open for a period of time, allowing the suspects to escape.
* A 62-year-old woman
was doused with petrol
and set alight at a four-digit gaming outlet in Taman Pusat Kepong, Kuala Lumpur on Aug 9. The woman was working as a teller when an unidentified man attacked her.
She suffered 50 per cent burns and is still treated in hospital where her condition is listed as critical but stable.
Police launched a hunt for the assailant and examined CCTV recordings around Taman Pusat Kepong to establish his movements and identity. By Aug 11, investigators
had recorded statements from about 20 people
in connection with the case.
The suspect is still at large and the motive could not be established. The victim's daughter had said her mother could have been a victim of mistaken identity.
* A dispute over oil palm fruit and farming equipment
led to the murder
of a 49-year-old Malaysian in Banting, Kuala Langat on Aug 9.
Family members who went looking for the victim found him dead in the plantation.
Investigators believed an argument involving stolen oil palm fruit and farming equipment had led to the attack on the victim.
Eight suspects, including foreigners, between the ages of 20 and 60, were arrested as investigators worked to reconstruct what happened at the plantation.
Police are now looking for an Indonesian man to assist in the investigations.

Title: Higher-than-expected growth on the cards for Malaysia [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia is expected to chalk economic growth of more than 5.0 per cent this year, beyond the 4.0 to 5.0 per cent estimate by Bank Negara Malaysia, following the better-than-expected gross domestic product (GDP) in the second quarter (Q2).
Economists contacted by Business Times said that the economy's resiliency against external shocks was the main reason for the outperformance, as well as strong demands for products ranging from electrical and electronics (E&E) to liquefied natural gas.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid raised his full-year 2026 growth forecast to 5.2 per cent from 4.8 per cent, after the Q2 economic expansion of 6.0 per cent surpassed the 5.8 per cent advanced estimate.
"The economic growth was robust and the country has been benefitting from strong external demand, namely in tech-related sectors such as electrical and electronics (E&E), as well as commodities such as liquefied natural gas (LNG) and tin," he said.
However, the strength in external demand contrasted with a more cautious domestic economy, noted Afzanizam.
Private investment moderated to 4.3 per cent in Q2 from 7.8 per cent in Q1, while private consumption grew 4.8 per cent, from 4.7 per cent in the preceding quarter.
Government spending provided additional support, with public consumption and public investment accelerating to 6.3 per cent and 7.6 per cent respectively, from 5.3 per cent and 4.1 per cent in Q1.
Afzanizam said private consumption had continued to grow below its longer-term trend of around six per cent, with higher living costs – seen from Malaysia's headline inflation that accelerated to 1.9 per cent in Q2 from 1.6 per cent in Q1 –  likely to keep consumers cautious in their spending.
Despite the stronger growth, Afzanizam expects the central bank to maintain the overnight policy rate (OPR) at 2.75 per cent.
"The prevailing monetary stance continues to remain supportive to growth while inflation dynamics are fairly contained at the moment," he said.
Meanwhile, Zafri Zulkeffeli, senior economist at Bank Islam Malaysia Bhd upgraded his 2026 GDP growth forecast to 5.5 per cent from 4.9 per cent, stating that Malaysia's growth momentum could strengthen further if agricultural output and export volumes return to sustained expansion, providing an additional boost alongside strong technology and commodity exports.
"Overall, the combination of resilient domestic demand, strong export momentum and
sustained private investment supports a more optimistic growth outlook for 2026," he stated in a report on Friday.
Socio-Economic Research Centre's executive director Lee Heng Guie meanwhile said the 6.0 per cent Q2 growth was in line with the centre's expectations, noting that the firm had raised its 2026 growth forecast to between 5.0 and 5.2 per cent earlier this month.
However, he said the headline figure masked an uneven recovery, reflecting a structural divergence between capital-intensive and technology-related sectors and parts of the domestic economy.
"Despite the strong headline GDP numbers, there were uneven growth reflecting a structural divergence where capital-intensive and tech sectors such as semiconductors, AI-driven data centres and high-end manufacturing outpace consumer-facing retail, domestic services and stagnant middle-income wage growth," he said.
EXPORT DEMAND AS KEY TEST FOR 2026 GDP EXPANSIONS
The economists' assessment follows official data showing Malaysia's economy expanded 6.0 per cent year-on-year in Q2, exceeding the 5.8 per cent advance estimate and accelerating from 5.4 per cent in Q1.
The economy grew 5.7 per cent in the first half of 2026.
On a quarter-on-quarter seasonally adjusted basis, GDP expanded 2.5 per cent in Q2, reversing a marginal contraction of 0.03 per cent in Q1.
The stronger performance was supported by resilient external demand, particularly for E&E products, while domestic demand continued to expand at a more measured pace.
For the remainder of 2026, economists said the key test would be whether strong export demand can be sustained while private consumption and investment regain momentum.
The outlook will also depend on global trade policies, geopolitical tensions, commodity prices and the performance of technology-related exports.
For now, the stronger-than-expected Q2 performance has improved the country's growth prospects and strengthened the case for a full-year expansion above five per cent.
For the second half of 2026, Lee expects GDP growth to moderate to between 4.5 and 5.0 per cent, compared with 5.7 per cent in the first half.
He attributed the expected moderation partly to a high base effect in the second half of 2025, as well as adjustments in stocks following the ramp-up in production and front-loading of exports during the initial energy shock and supply-chain disruptions.
"The manufacturing sector still remains the prime mover, underpinned by the E&E sector and also domestic-market-oriented industries such as transport equipment and construction-related building materials," he said.
FINANCING CONDITIONS REMAINS SUPPORTIVE
Meanwhile, financing conditions remained supportive, with credit growth to the private non-financial sector accelerating to 6.4 per cent in Q2 from 5.6 per cent in Q1.
Bank Negara governor Datuk Seri Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour said the stronger credit growth was particularly evident among businesses, with business loan growth accelerating to 7.2 per cent from 5.7 per cent previously.
Corporate bond financing also expanded by 8.1 per cent in Q2, compared with 5.9 per cent in Q1, amid higher issuances for working capital needs.
Household loan growth, meanwhile, remained broadly stable at 5.4 per cent, compared with 5.5 per cent in the previous quarter.
The data suggest that while private investment growth moderated, overall financing conditions continued to provide support to businesses and the wider economy.
The stronger Q2 performance also gives BNM greater flexibility to keep monetary policy unchanged, particularly as inflation remains relatively contained.
Lee of SERC said stronger GDP growth could strengthen the case for normalisation of the OPR, but expects BNM to keep the rate at 2.75 per cent for now while monitoring the inflation trajectory.
He expects inflation to range between 2.0 and 2.5 per cent.
Meanwhile, senior ASEAN economist at HSBC, Yun Liu, commented that Malaysia is benefiting significantly from the AI wave.
"Amid the AI tech upswing, whoever gets the electronics supply chain controls the trade and sees strong growth," said Yun, noting that Malaysia's 5.7 per cent growth in the first half of 2026 placed it as the third-fastest growing economy in Southeast Asia behind Vietnam and Singapore.
Yun also noted that Bank Negara can afford to hold a "wait and see" stance on its monetary policy, despite increasing global macro uncertainty.
