Title: PKR Youth backs UUCA repeal, urges students to speak up for wider reforms
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 15 — PKR Youth today backed Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s announcement to repeal the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (UUCA), but said the move should pave the way for wider reforms to strengthen university autonomy, academic freedom and student rights.
The party’s youth wing also urged students to continue speaking up and acting as a check and balance on the government, despite being part of Anwar’s own party.
“To Malaysian students, do not stop speaking up. Do not stop thinking. Do not stop being a check and balance on the country,” PKR Youth chief Muhammad Kamil Abdul Munim said in a statement today.
Kamil said the repeal should open the way for stronger university autonomy, academic freedom, freedom of association and freedom of expression, as well as greater space for students to determine the direction of their own movements.
He said university freedom should not be interpreted as freedom without responsibility, but should allow campuses to manage differences through knowledge, argument and dialogue.
Kamil said universities should produce graduates who were willing to question established norms, challenge conventional thinking and defend what they believed was right responsibly.
PKR Youth described Anwar’s announcement as an important milestone in the decades-long struggle by Malaysian students for freer and more democratic campuses.
Kamil said the government’s decision recognised that students should not be shaped by a culture of fear and excessive control, but trusted to think, debate, disagree, criticise and offer solutions for the country.
He said students and young Malaysians should view the development as proof that reform required political courage, patience and sustained support to turn announcements into meaningful change.
Kamil also called on the Madani government to continue pursuing institutional reforms, saying students should remain among the key forces monitoring, pressing for and helping to implement those changes.
The call for students to remain a check and balance is notable as PKR Youth is part of Anwar’s own party, even as it backs his decision to repeal UUCA.
Kamil said reform did not end with a single announcement or the repeal of one law, with further changes still needed in higher education and other institutions.
He urged Malaysian students to continue voicing their views, thinking critically and holding the country’s institutions to account.
Anwar announced the repeal of UUCA at the 2026 PKR National Congress in Ayer Keroh today, saying previous amendments had given students greater freedom but had not addressed all their concerns.
UUCA, introduced in 1971, has been amended seven times, including changes in 2012 that allowed students to participate in political party activities outside campus.
The latest amendments in 2024 included changes to student disciplinary procedures, with such matters at public universities shifted from the vice-chancellor to Student Disciplinary Committees, as well as expanded powers for student representative councils and student bodies to collect funds and receive contributions subject to prevailing laws and regulations.

Title: Anwar announces special Madani F1 tickets for MyKad holders from RM200
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 15 — Malaysians holding MyKad will be able to attend all three days of Formula 1’s return to Sepang through special Tiket Madani priced from RM200, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced today.
He said the initiative would give more Malaysians the opportunity to experience Formula 1 in person when the race returns to Sepang in October.
“Alhamdulillah, following discussions and agreement with Bahrain, the government is pleased to announce special Madani Tickets for MyKad holders priced from as little as RM200 for access throughout the three-day event,” he said in a Facebook post today.
The Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix at the Sepang International Circuit is scheduled for October 2 to 4, marking the sport’s return to Malaysia for the first time since 2017.
Tickets announced earlier this week included three-day passes for Malaysian citizens ranging from RM200 for the G Hillstand to RM2,083.40 for the Main Grandstand.
Anwar said the initiative was aimed at giving more Malaysians the chance to experience Formula 1 directly at Sepang.
“Hopefully, this initiative will give more Malaysians the opportunity to experience Formula 1 in person at Sepang,” he said.
Further details on the Madani Tickets will be announced by SIC soon, he added.

Title: Anwar says allocations for Sabah, Sarawak, Kedah and Kelantan increased under Madani govt
Article:
MELAKA, Aug 15 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today dismissed claims by certain quarters that the Madani Government is sidelining several states.
Instead, he stressed that allocations to each state differ according to priorities and have continued to increase under his administration.
“Sabah’s expenditure has increased by 35 per cent in the three years since we took over the government. Before that, in the preceding years, did the state government raise the issue? No... Allocations for Sabah, Sarawak, Kedah and Kelantan have increased overall.
“Terengganu’s allocation rose from RM6 billion in 2022 to RM8.1 billion this year, as did Perlis, Johor and others. Johor’s allocation increased from RM10.2 billion in 2022 to RM14.6 billion in 2026,” he said when delivering his Presidential Policy Speech at the 2026 PKR National Congress at the Melaka International Trade Centre (MITC) in Ayer Keroh here today.
Anwar said the Federal allocation to Sabah had also increased by 35 per cent, from RM13 billion in 2022 to RM17.6 billion in 2026, while Sarawak’s allocation rose from RM10.2 billion in 2022 to RM15.1 billion, an increase of 48 per cent. — Bernama

Title: Missing three days, found 140km away, back with families but KL police still investigating case of two Alor Gajah MRSM students
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 15 — Two 16-year-old MRSM Alor Gajah students who went missing for three days have been reunited with their families.
Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said the two teenagers were found at about 10.30pm yesterday at Central Market here — nearly 140km away from the Melaka school campus.
“The cause and circumstances surrounding the incident are still under police investigation,” he was quoted by Berita Harian as saying today.
The students, Siti Nur Aaira Aidi and Nur Aisy Humaira Mohd Saad, were reported missing after a teacher lodged a police report at 10.46pm on August 11.
Fadil said the two had previously sought treatment at a health clinic in Alor Gajah after feeling unwell.
“They were taken to Hospital Kuala Lumpur after being found for further medical examination before being handed back to their families,” he added.
MARA chairman Datuk Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki took to Facebook yesterday appealing for public assistance to pray for the safe return of the two students, later reporting that the girls had been found by police.

Title: Not all of Umno can be guilty: Pakatan Harapan should not use an overly generic approach – Phar Kim Beng
Article:
AUGUST 15 — One of the greatest dangers in Malaysian politics is the temptation to convert institutional wrongdoing into collective political guilt.
This is particularly important when Pakatan Harapan (PH) discusses Umno and the controversies associated with previous Barisan Nasional administrations.
The principle should be straightforward: not all of Umno can be guilty simply because some Umno leaders, office-holders or political appointees may have been implicated in wrongdoing.
If Malaysia is serious about becoming a mature constitutional democracy, responsibility must be compartmentalised. Investigations must identify particular decisions, particular offices, particular individuals and particular periods. Evidence must determine culpability. Political affiliation cannot substitute for proof.
This distinction becomes especially important when Malaysia confronts controversies involving institutions such as Tabung Haji, Felda, the Littoral Combat Ship programme and other episodes of alleged financial or administrative malfeasance.
Where wrongdoing occurred, it should be investigated rigorously. Where criminal liability can be established, prosecution should follow. Where administrative negligence occurred, institutional reforms should be undertaken.
But none of these propositions logically establishes the guilt of an entire political party consisting of millions of members and generations of leaders.
Umno is not one person.
Nor is Umno one administration, one faction or one historical episode.
The writer says that Umno is not one person, adding that accountability for alleged wrongdoing should be directed at specific individuals and decisions rather than applied collectively to all members. — Picture by Yusof Mat Isa
It contains reformists and conservatives, government leaders and backbenchers, veterans and younger members, federal and state politicians, as well as ordinary members who could not conceivably have known what senior officials were doing inside ministries, government-linked companies or statutory bodies.
To treat them as collectively responsible would reproduce precisely the kind of politics PH has long argued Malaysia should transcend.
There is also a constitutional principle involved. Malaysia’s criminal justice system recognises individual culpability. A person is not guilty because of association.
Political parties themselves may face legal consequences under appropriate circumstances, but the misconduct of particular office-holders cannot automatically be transferred to every member of an organisation.
The distinction between political responsibility, administrative responsibility and criminal responsibility must therefore remain clear.
Political responsibility can be broad. A government can legitimately be criticised for allowing poor governance to flourish under its watch.
Ministers can be held politically accountable for failures within their portfolios even when they did not personally commit criminal offences.
Criminal responsibility, however, requires something much more specific.
Who authorised the transaction? Who knew about it? Who benefited? Who concealed information? Who ignored professional warnings? Who exercised fiduciary responsibility? Who violated the law?
These are evidentiary questions. They cannot be answered merely by saying “Umno.”
This is why PH should be particularly careful about using overly generic language when discussing previous scandals. PH presently governs Malaysia through a coalition arrangement in which Barisan Nasional is an important partner.
If PH simultaneously depends upon Umno for governmental stability while rhetorically portraying Umno as collectively responsible for every historical controversy associated with BN governments, it creates a contradiction that will eventually become politically unsustainable.
There must instead be legal compartmentalisation.
Those who committed offences should answer for them. Those who facilitated wrongdoing should be investigated.
Those who failed in their fiduciary responsibilities should explain themselves. Those who attempted to obstruct investigations should face the appropriate consequences.
But those who were not involved must not be politically convicted through association.
Indeed, this approach can strengthen rather than weaken the campaign against corruption.
When accusations become excessively broad, the genuinely culpable can hide within the collective.
They can claim that investigations are merely partisan attacks against Umno, Malays or previous governments.
Specificity removes that defence.
A forensic approach says something very different: this is not an attack against Umno.
It is an investigation into particular decisions made by identifiable individuals under particular legal responsibilities.
That distinction is enormously important.
It also creates space for Umno itself to support institutional cleansing. Party members who had nothing to do with past misconduct should have every reason to support investigations that distinguish them from those responsible.
Indeed, Umno’s long-term rehabilitation may depend partly upon its willingness to accept such differentiation.
PH should therefore resist transforming accountability into political demonisation.
Malaysia cannot progress by replacing one form of partisan triumphalism with another.
The country needs institutions capable of distinguishing between allegation and evidence, negligence and criminality, political responsibility and legal liability.
This becomes even more important as Malaysia approaches another electoral cycle. If every controversy is converted into collective condemnation, politics becomes an endless process of mutually assured accusation.
Umno blames DAP. PAS blames DAP and PH. PH blames Umno or PN.
Each political organisation then constructs an entire community of villains.
Such politics eventually destroys the centre.
Malaysia needs the opposite: accountability without collective persecution and reconciliation without impunity.
PH therefore has an opportunity to establish a higher standard. It should insist that every credible allegation of corruption, abuse of power or institutional malfeasance be investigated thoroughly while simultaneously rejecting the proposition that membership of a political party constitutes evidence of wrongdoing.
This principle must apply equally to Umno, PKR, DAP, Amanah, Bersatu, PAS or any other political organisation.
No party should receive immunity.
But no party should be subjected to collective guilt either.
The rule of law becomes meaningful precisely when it refuses both extremes.
Malaysia does not need fewer investigations. It needs better investigations: forensic, independent, evidence-driven and directed towards those actually responsible.
Not all of Umno can possibly be guilty of every wrongdoing associated with governments in which Umno once played the dominant role.
PH should understand this distinction clearly. The objective must be to isolate wrongdoing, prosecute culpability and repair institutions – not to criminalise an entire political tradition.
That is not merely good coalition politics.
It is the essence of constitutional government.
* Phar Kim Beng is professor of Asean Studies, and director at the Institute of International and Asean Studies, International Islamic University Malaysia.

Title: Anwar on Tabung Haji RCI findings: ‘RM12b was lost, isn’t that sakau?’
Article:
MELAKA, Aug 15 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has stressed that acts of “sakau” (siphoning of funds) did occur in Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH), following the loss of billions of ringgit as highlighted in the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on the institution.
The Finance Minister said the term “sakau” should not be avoided or questioned if the facts showed that money had been lost from an institution entrusted with managing the savings of Muslims.
“Some people do not like the term ‘sakau’. I want to repeat here in Melaka that there was indeed ‘sakau’ in Tabung Haji. RM12 billion was lost, isn’t that ‘sakau’? There was indeed ‘sakau’,” he said when delivering his Presidential Policy Speech at the 2026 Keadilan National Congress here today.
Anwar said action must be taken against those responsible regardless of their position or political background, as the consequences of the actions of a few individuals ultimately had to be borne by the people as a whole.
“Only some were involved in the ‘sakau’, but the ones who had to pay and bear the burden were all Malaysians, regardless of race or religion,” he said.
The Prime Minister said firmness in taking action should not be construed as political vengeance, adding that he himself would face criticism whether he acted or refrained from acting.
He said some individuals who were supposedly intelligent and highly educated appeared to be firm in fighting corruption and abuse of power, but this was merely hypocrisy because any action that did not favour those they supported would be labelled as revenge.
“Although they may appear intelligent, it is actually full of hypocrisy because when we do not take action, you say we are slow, but when we take action, you call it revenge,” Anwar said.
Meanwhile, the Prime Minister said His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim. King of Malaysia, had also decreed that efforts to uncover weaknesses in the management of institutions involving the people’s interests should not stop with TH.
He said that after the TH issue was resolved, attention would be turned to the Federal Land Consolidation and Rehabilitation Authority (Felda), in line with the government’s responsibility to ensure that people’s institutions were managed transparently and responsibly.
Anwar stressed that a more stringent enforcement process would begin now to ensure that those who committed wrongdoing were held accountable, regardless of their position, party or influence.
— Bernama

Title: Anwar announces repeal of Universities and University Colleges Act, after students push for greater freedom
Article:
AYER KEROH, Aug 15 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today announced that the government will repeal the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (UUCA), following continued calls from students for greater freedom.
Anwar, who is also PKR president, said the decision came after several amendments to the Act failed to address all concerns raised by university students, local media reported.
“University students feel that they should be free. We have given them greater freedom through amendments to the UUCA (previously), but there are still some who are dissatisfied, and they have submitted a memorandum,” he said in his policy speech at the 2026 PKR National Congress at the Melaka International Trade Centre here.
“So today, I want to announce that we will repeal the Act.”
The announcement marks a significant shift from the government’s previous approach of amending UUCA to give students greater freedom while retaining the law as the framework for public university governance.
UUCA has been amended several times since it was introduced in 1971, including changes in 2012 that allowed students to participate in political party activities outside campus.
The latest amendments, passed in 2024, included changes to student disciplinary procedures and financial management, including allowing student representative councils and student bodies to collect money and receive contributions subject to prevailing laws and regulations.
In 2023, Anwar had said sections of UUCA restricting the freedom of students and academics would be repealed, while the Higher Education Ministry said at the time that it intended to retain the Act but amend it to give students greater freedom in political activities.
The 2024 amendments also shifted disciplinary decisions involving public university students from the vice-chancellor to Student Disciplinary Committees through amendments to Section 16B.
The amendments further revised Section 15A to allow student representative councils and student bodies to raise funds and receive contributions, subject to applicable written laws and regulations.
UUCA, enacted in 1971, provides the legal framework for the governance and administration of public universities in Malaysia.
Student groups have for years called for the Act to be repealed, particularly provisions they say restrict student participation in politics and public affairs, with Anwar himself previously pledging to remove sections that limited student and academic freedom.
The government’s 2024 amendments had instead focused on improving university governance, student activities and disciplinary procedures while retaining UUCA as the governing framework.

Title: Woman rescued by public after falling from Darul Hana Bridge in Kuching
Article:
KUCHING, Aug 15 — A woman was rescued by members of the public after falling from the Darul Hana Bridge at Kuching Waterfront here yesterday evening.
Kuching district police chief ACP Alexson Naga Chabu confirmed the incident, saying the woman had been admitted to Sarawak General Hospital (SGH) for further treatment at the Yellow Zone of the Emergency and Trauma Unit.
“Initial investigations found that the incident was related to a personal issue — however, investigations are ongoing to determine the root cause of the incident.
“As such, the public is urged to refrain from speculating or spreading unverified information regarding the incident,” he said in a statement today.
Those with information related to the incident may contact the Kuching district police headquarters at 082-244444 or the investigating officer, Insp Logeswara, at 018-2914239.
Videos of the incident were circulated on various Facebook pages yesterday evening, showing the woman being rescued by members of the public.
Those experiencing emotional problems are encouraged to contact trained volunteers at Befrienders by calling 03-76272929 (24 hours). — Bernama

Title: Sibu latest to record unhealthy API as nine Sarawak areas affected
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 15 — Sibu is the latest area in Sarawak to record an unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) reading, bringing the total number of locations in that category to nine as of 9am today.
According to data from the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, Kuching recorded the highest reading at 167, followed by Samarahan (164), Serian (163), Sarikei (157), Bintulu (156), Sri Aman (154), Mukah (152), Sibu (131), and Samalaju (126).
Meanwhile, 46 areas nationwide recorded moderate API readings, while 13 areas recorded good air quality.
API readings from 0 to 50 indicate good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy, and readings above 300 are hazardous.
API data is released hourly from 68 air quality monitoring stations nationwide. — Bernama

Title: After Tabung Haji, Anwar says King wants Felda probe next
Article:
MELAKA, Aug 15 — The government will investigate issues involving Felda after completing its probe into alleged misappropriation at Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH), Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today.
The move follows a directive from His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, the King of Malaysia, for investigations into institutions owned by the people to go beyond TH, The Star quoted Anwar as saying at the PKR Congress in Melaka.
“The King told me last week that do not let it end with TH, (but) continue,” Anwar said in his policy speech.
Anwar said the King had specifically asked who was currently in charge of Felda, to which he replied that he was responsible for the agency.
“His Majesty also asked who is in charge of Felda now. I answered, me, (so) once TH is done, uncover what happened at Felda,” he said.
Anwar, who is also PKR president, said the government will not compromise with anyone found to have breached regulations or taken public assets.
He said the action was not to target certain parties, but to obtain certainty on the land development agency that previously carried a heavy debt burden.
“Let the enforcement agencies investigate professionally," he said.
Anwar, who is also the Pakatan Harapan chairman, said the authorities must be firm and take action, regardless of the position of the individual being investigated.
He made it clear that any action taken should not be seen as a desperate retaliatory act, but a more stringent process without any compromises.
Earlier this year, Anwar said the federal government is burdened with Felda’s debt of almost RM1 billion a year, which was allegedly due to a weak administrative management.
He said that the responsibility of paying off the financial commitment now had to be shouldered by his administration to ensure that the survival and welfare of the settlers were not affected.
Anwar said the government continues to strengthen the reform agenda to stop the practice of embezzlement, in addition to ensuring that development can be enjoyed more fairly by the people.
He said that efforts to save the country from such disruptive practices must be followed by improving the administrative system and process so that wealth is not excessively distributed to certain parties.
“In these three years, we have ensured political stability, maintained security and a growing economy.
“Now, we must continue to strengthen the reform agenda in several areas that are still pending,” he said.

Title: Registration opens for LHDN’s Budget 2027 taxation seminar
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 15 — Registration is now open for the National Taxation Seminar 2026 (Budget 2027), which will provide updates on taxation developments and Budget 2027 proposals through two online sessions on October 14 and 21.
In a statement yesterday, the Inland Revenue Board of Malaysia (LHDN) said the seminar was organised in conjunction with the tabling of Budget 2027, scheduled for October 2026.
The seminar will be held in two sessions, with Session 1 on October 14 (Wednesday) and Session 2 on October 21 (Wednesday), via Zoom.
“The seminar brings together experienced taxation speakers and panellists comprising senior officials from the Ministry of Finance, LHDN, the Chartered Tax Institute of Malaysia and the Malaysian Association of Tax Accountants,” it said.
Key topics include the Budget 2027 proposals, the Special Programme for Voluntary Disclosure on e-Invoicing and Stamp Duty: Identify the Instrument, Determine the Duty Correctly.
LHDN said the seminar would also focus on taxation developments, changes and current issues of importance to taxpayers, tax practitioners, accounting bodies and the professional community.
Registration is now open through the SPK portal at [https://heal.hasil.gov.my/](https://heal.hasil.gov.my/).
Employers registered with the Human Resources Development Corporation (HRD Corp) may also claim training costs for SPK 2026 participants, subject to the stipulated conditions.
Registered employers interested in doing so only need to select “Non-Registered Training Provider Details - Government” under the Training Assistance Scheme when applying for the training grant.
For enquiries and feedback, contact the LHDN Contact Centre at 03-8911 1000 or +603-8911 1000 for calls from overseas, use LHDN Live Chat or submit the customer feedback form through the official LHDN portal. — Bernama

Title: Perlis gets new acting police chief as predecessor moves to Bukit Aman
Article:
KANGAR, Aug 15 — Perlis deputy police chief SAC Zaihairul Idrus has been appointed as acting state police chief, effective yesterday.
He succeeds Datuk Muhammad Abdul Halim, who will assume his new role as deputy director (Movement/Operations) at Bukit Aman’s Department of Internal Security and Public Order (KDNKA) after leading the Perlis police contingent for two years and eight months.
The handover ceremony was witnessed by Bukit Aman KDNKA director Datuk Seri Mohd Yusri Hassan Basri and held at the Perlis contingent police headquarters (IPK) here yesterday.
Speaking to reporters after the ceremony, Zaihairul said he would continue the efforts, including welfare initiatives, implemented by Muhammad during his tenure as the state police chief.
In addition, Zaihairul said he would strengthen close cooperation with Bukit Aman in efforts to address any security issues in the state, which borders Thailand.
“Perlis’ position as a state bordering a neighbouring country requires continued cooperation between the Perlis contingent and Bukit Aman to strengthen security in border areas.
“I believe that with close cooperation with Bukit Aman, the crime rate in the Perlis police contingent will decline even more significantly,” he said. — Bernama

Title: PKFZ chairman says Chinese-linked cargo presence alone isn’t evidence of trade fraud, after US report flagging Malaysia
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 15 — The Port Klang Free Zone (PKFZ) today rejected any suggestion that the presence of Chinese-linked businesses or cargo at its facility is evidence of tariff evasion, following a new US report that places Malaysia among economies facing elevated risks of illegal transshipment.
PKFZ chairman Lim Lip Eng said the free zone operated within a regulated customs and trade compliance framework and did not facilitate or endorse false declarations, misrepresentation of origin or circumvention of international trade measures.
“Therefore, the presence of Chinese-linked businesses or international cargo within a Malaysian free zone should not, in itself, be interpreted as evidence of tariff evasion or illegal transshipment,” he said in a statement.
Lim said all investors, manufacturers, traders and logistics operators seeking to establish operations at PKFZ were subject to screening, due diligence and regulatory requirements under Malaysian law and free-zone regulations.
He said matters involving the origin of goods and export certification were handled by the relevant national authorities rather than PKFZ.
For US-bound exports, the Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry (Miti) has been the sole issuer of Non-Preferential Certificates of Origin since May 6 last year with the certification process requiring supporting documents including cost analyses, statutory declarations, manufacturing information and raw-material records.
“PKFZ also welcomes greater scrutiny and stronger enforcement against genuine cases of trade fraud,” Lim said.
He added that a transparent and properly regulated trading environment would protect legitimate investors and strengthen Malaysia’s position as a regional logistics and manufacturing hub.
He said PKFZ would cooperate with Miti, Customs and other relevant authorities if there were regulatory concerns or indications of non-compliance.
Lim’s remarks come after a US report, titled
The Great Transshipment Scam
, examines the rerouting of goods through third countries to avoid higher US tariffs, particularly involving Chinese-origin goods, and outlines measures Washington is taking to detect and penalise such practices.
The report by the US Office of Trade and Manufacturing Policy identified more than 40 economies as being associated with elevated illegal transshipment risk, with Malaysia placed in its second tier alongside Brazil, Indonesia, Thailand, Türkiye and Vietnam.
The report said Tier 2 economies had significant trade volumes involving China-linked goods and deeper integration with Chinese supply chains, manufacturing platforms and logistics networks, while stressing that the trade flows also included legitimate activity.
It said the US had seen a shift in import sourcing since tariffs on Chinese goods were introduced in 2018, with China’s direct share of US goods imports declining while the combined share supplied by the identified transshipment-risk economies increased.
However, the report acknowledged that the shift did not establish that all displaced Chinese trade had been illegally transshipped, noting that some reflected legitimate changes in production, investment and sourcing.
The report estimated a central annual illegal transshipment flow of about US$75 billion (RM306.44 billion), with associated US federal revenue losses estimated at US$19 billion to US$26 billion (RM77.63 billion to RM106.23 billion), although it stressed that the figures were model-based estimates rather than observed losses.
The US administration said it was developing an AI-enabled “Detective Border” system to help Customs and Border Protection analyse shipment data, routing histories, product classifications, ownership links and other indicators to identify high-risk shipments and distinguish legitimate foreign investment from illegal pass-through trade.

Title: Police confirm body found inside suitcase in Sungai Perak is female
Article:
IPOH, Aug 15 — Police have confirmed that the body discovered inside a suitcase in Sungai Perak near the Lembah Kuala Kangsar jetty yesterday afternoon is that of a woman.
Kuala Kangsar police chief ACP Heisham Harun said preliminary investigations found that the victim is approximately 30 years old, though her identity has yet to be determined.
He said police received a call from a man at 3.12pm, reporting that he had found the body in the river near the jetty.
“The body has been sent to Taiping Hospital for an autopsy. The case is being investigated under Section 302 of the Penal Code for murder,” he said in a statement.
Meanwhile, Heisham advised the public not to speculate or provoke any unrest regarding the case.
He appealed to anyone with information to come forward and assist with the investigation by contacting the Kuala Kangsar District Police Headquarters at 05-776 2222 or any nearby police station. — Bernama

Title: Brother checks in on sister at her Sungai Petani shop, only to find her body
Article:
SUNGAI PETANI, Aug 15 — A 77-year-old retired pharmacist went to a shop in Pekan Sungai Lalang here to see his younger sister, only to discover her body after noticing a foul smell coming from the premises.
Kuala Muda district police chief Assistant Commissioner Hanyan Ramlan said the man arrived at the shop at about 6pm and became suspicious after detecting the smell from inside.
“He then contacted the police for assistance,” Hanyan was quoted as saying by
Harian Metro
last night.
The woman, aged 69, was believed to have been living alone at the shop.
Her body was taken to the Forensic Unit at Sultan Abdul Halim Hospital in Kedah for a post-mortem.
Police have classified the case as sudden death pending the post-mortem report.

Title: PKR Youth chief urges elected reps to get closer to grassroots ahead of elections
Article:
MELAKA, Aug 15 — Elected leaders need to build strong networks with the community at the grassroots level to ensure that relationships with the people are always maintained, said Angkatan Muda Keadilan (AMK) chief Muhammad Kamil Abdul Munim.
He said close relationships with the community were also important to enable leaders and party to convey the right narrative, thus warding off negative perceptions that may be created by the other side.
“Our presence is important, our narrative is important, our machinery is important, our communication is important. Community relations and our networks at the grassroots level are also important,” he said when wrapping up the debate on the AMK Chief’s Policy Address in conjunction with 2026 AMK National Congress here yesterday.
Muhammad Kamil said preparations for the election should not only focus on the narrative at the national level, but also take into account issues and needs of the community at the local level.
In the meantime, he urged leaders at the local level to increase programmes and activities with members at the grassroots level, especially new members to instil an understanding of the party’s ideals and struggles.
He said the effort was important to ensure members understood their duties and responsibilities and the reasons for choosing the party’s platform for struggle.
“There was no effort to polish idealism, to make our new members understand the duties and responsibilities and the reasons why we are here and have chosen this platform for struggle.
“This is what we fear, that in the end we may slowly deviate from the path of this struggle,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Hamzah: BN-Perikatan seat talks must go beyond Melaka, allow room for compromise
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 15 — Barisan Nasional (BN) and Perikatan Nasional (PN) should work out a nationwide seat allocation formula and be prepared to make concessions if their electoral cooperation is to last, Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin said in an interview with news outlet
Free Malaysia Today.
The Parti Wawasan president said the two coalitions could not limit negotiations to the coming Melaka election or simply insist on defending seats they currently hold.
“If we want to cooperate, it cannot be a matter of pick and choose,” he said in the interview published today.
Parti Wawasan is a component of PN, having been admitted into the coalition in June with the backing of PAS.
Hamzah said the approach should instead take into account the strengths and weaknesses of both coalitions across the country, with incumbency used as a starting point but improved through a more flexible formula.
He said this was necessary to ensure the arrangement gave confidence to BN and PN leaders and supporters nationwide, rather than benefiting only certain parties or states.
“If we only look at where we stand today (seats currently held by each coalition), of course we would want to defend it so that no one else can take over,” he said.
“But if we look at the bigger goal, we need to sit down, compromise and make concessions,” he added.
Hamzah said BN and PN should also consider states where Umno currently holds no state seats if they intend to extend their cooperation nationwide.
His remarks come after BN and PN worked together in the August 1 Negeri Sembilan election, winning 25 of the state’s 36 seats.
The latest push for broader cooperation comes as the Melaka state election is expected to be called before the state assembly’s term expires at the end of December.
Hamzah said the two coalitions had previously been part of the same federal governments under Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin and Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob, but those arrangements were not based on advance planning.
He said future cooperation should instead begin with a common agenda and clearly defined roles, including a shared goal of developing the country and benefiting Malaysians.

Title: Selangor Sultan urges Muslims to show compassion towards all animals, including strays
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Aug 15 — The Sultan of Selangor, Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah, has called on Muslims to always do good and show compassion towards all animals, including strays and wildlife.
In line with the Friday sermon titled ‘Ihsan Terhadap Mahkluk Allah SWT’ (compassion towards Allah SWT’s creatures) delivered at mosques throughout Selangor yesterday, His Royal Highness also called on the people to reflect on and understand its contents.
In a post on the Selangor Royal Office’s Facebook page, His Royal Highness said that as stewards of the earth, humans bear a great responsibility to care for, protect and manage the environment responsibly, including animals, plants, hills, seas and rivers.
“All these are signs of the greatness of Allah SWT, and their sustainability must be protected and preserved.
Sultan Sharafuddin also said that the relationship between humans and other creatures should always be built on the principles of compassion and responsibility.
His Royal Highness said Prophet Muhammad placed great emphasis on compassion towards animals, and Islam teaches its followers to treat animals well by providing them with food and water, or at the very least, not mistreating any animal created by Allah.
However, Sultan Sharafuddin said the situation is different when wildlife poses a threat to public safety or cause damage to property.
“In such circumstances, Islam allows action to be taken to prevent harm, which is in line with the objectives of the Maqasid Syariah, namely protecting life and property,” the post said.
The Ruler said showing compassion towards animals and ensuring human safety were not contradictory, but rather both were part of the beauty of Islamic teachings, which place everything in its proper context. — Bernama

Title: DPM Fadillah recovering well after successful double heart bypass surgery at IJN
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 15 — Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof, who is also Energy Transition and Water Transformation Minister (Petra), is recovering well after undergoing successful double coronary artery bypass surgery at the National Heart Institute (IJN) on Wednesday.
In a statement yesterday, the Office of the Deputy Prime Minister said Fadillah’s family expressed their deepest appreciation to the IJN medical team for its commitment, expertise and professional care throughout his treatment.
“Thank you to the ministries, mosques and surau, houses of worship, government and private agencies, non-governmental organisations, family, friends and all Malaysians who have continuously prayed for his recovery and given him their support,” it said.
Meanwhile, IJN in a separate statement said Fadillah continues to show positive progress following a successful coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) procedure on August 12, after being admitted to the institute on July 28 and undergoing a coronary angiogram the following day.
“He underwent a coronary angiogram on July 29. Following a multidisciplinary team discussion, the medical team determined that coronary artery bypass surgery was the most appropriate course of treatment.
“The double bypass surgery was performed on August 12 by IJN Senior Consultant Cardiothoracic Surgeons Prof Datuk Seri Dr Mohamed Ezani Md Taib and Prof Datuk Seri Dr Mond Azhan Yakub, together with Clinical Fellow Cardiothoracic and Vascular Surgery Dr Ahmad Mahir Shamsuddin,” the statement said.
The surgery was carried out under IJN’s Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) protocol, a multidisciplinary approach designed to support early mobilisation, minimise complications, and promote a safer and faster recovery.
According to IJN Group Chief Executive Officer Prof Datuk Seri Dr Mohamed Ezani Md Taib the medical team is pleased with the Deputy Prime Minister’s progress, as his treatment and recovery have proceeded according to plan, and his condition continues to improve as expected.
“As part of his early mobilisation programme on August 13, the Deputy Prime Minister successfully completed 2.8 kilometres of cycling exercise under the supervision of IJN’s clinical team.
“He was subsequently transferred from the Intensive Care Unit to the general ward that afternoon, where he continues his post-CABG cardiac rehabilitation,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Police believe mother and son killed in Temerloh fuel tanker crash, DNA test underway
Article:
KUANTAN, Aug 15 — The police believe that the two victims who were burnt to death after the car they were travelling in was involved in a crash with a fuel tanker at Kilometre 9 of Jalan Temerloh-Triang this afternoon are a mother and son.
Temerloh District Police chief ACP Mohd Nasyim Bahron said the driver and passenger of the Perodua Bezza were believed to be a 39-year-old woman and her 12-year-old son, who were pronounced dead at the scene.
“The identities of both victims will be confirmed through comparison of DNA samples from their next-of-kin,” he said in a statement yesterday.
Meanwhile, he said preliminary investigations found that a tanker carrying 32,000 litres of diesel from Seremban to Temerloh was believed to have skidded into the opposite lane.
“Based on information from the victims’ next-of-kin, the car was travelling from Jerantut to Seremban. The collision caused the tanker trailer to crush the car, and both vehicles caught fire,” he said.
Mohd Nasyim said the 37-year-old lorry driver, however, managed to escape and sustained only minor injuries.
Meanwhile, he said post-mortem examinations on the victims would be conducted today. — Bernama

Title: Declared as chairs and underwear, but Customs finds 1,240 sex toys in Port Klang container instead
Article:
KLANG, Aug 15 — Customs officers got more than they bargained for when they opened a container at North Port Free Zone here and found 1,240 sex toys among its contents.
The shipment, which also contained other items, was seized after arriving in Malaysia from another Asian country on May 21, with the sex toys estimated to be worth about RM52,500, The Star reported.
“The items in the container were falsely declared as chairs, waist bags, stainless steel tumblers and underwear to avoid detection,” Selangor Customs Department director Noraidah Ishak told a news conference at the department headquarters here yesterday.
She said investigations were underway to identify the intended recipient of the shipment, adding that the haul was the department’s first seizure of sex toys this year.
“We believe the items were intended for the local market,” she added.
The department also detected more than RM40 million worth of contraband in three separate operations involving illegal waste, liquor and cigarettes.
Noraidah said the department seized 57 containers of illegal waste in the first half of this year, comprising 351,185kg of metal scrap in 13 containers and 841,552.50kg of plastic scrap in 44 containers.
“Checks showed that 13 containers had 351,185kg of metal scrap and 44 containers held 841,552.50kg of plastic scrap. All containers had no import permits,” she said.
The waste, estimated to be worth about RM5 million including duties and taxes, had been declared as copper concentrate and aluminium materials.
In another case, Customs seized a container carrying 1,578 litres of liquor hidden among auto parts, which arrived at Port Klang on April 27.
With the unpaid duties, the alcohol was estimated to be worth RM409,917, Noraidah said.
In the third case, eight containers seized on June 3 and 10 were found to contain 48.78 million cigarettes, valued to be worth RM37,560,600 with duties and taxes added.

Title: Tanker carrying 32,000 litres of fuel crashes into car in Temerloh, two occupants feared burnt
Article:
KUANTAN, Aug 15 — A fuel tanker carrying 32,000 litres of diesel and petrol crashed into a car at KM9 Jalan Temerloh-Triang yesterday, causing both vehicles to burst into flames, with two occupants of the car feared burnt.
Temerloh police chief ACP Mohd Nasyim Bahron said police received information from the public on the incident at about 4.30pm.
“Initial investigations found that the tanker, travelling from Seremban, Negeri Sembilan to Temerloh, was believed to have lost control and entered the opposite lane before crashing into the car.
“The collision caused both vehicles to catch fire. However, the 37-year-old tanker driver managed to escape and suffered only minor injuries,” he said when contacted.
Mohd Nasyim said the identities and number of victims in the car had yet to be confirmed due to the condition of the wreckage, while firefighting operations took time as the incident involved fuel.
He said the tanker driver would be detained to assist investigations under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987. — Bernama

Title: Anwar: PKR must remain a mass movement, not just a vehicle to win elections
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 15 — Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) must continue to serve as a mass movement that upholds integrity, social justice, unity and the people’s trust, rather than merely a vehicle for winning elections, its president Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.
In a Facebook post yesterday, the Prime Minister said these principles were crucial in efforts to build a more dignified, prosperous and just Malaysia for all.
Wishing delegates a meaningful PKR National Congress 2026, Anwar said he hoped the gathering would serve as a platform for introspection, allowing the party to assess its achievements and strengthen its resolve to carry forward the Reformasi agenda.
“May Allah SWT bless all our efforts for our beloved homeland, Insya-Allah,” he said.
The two-day PKR National Congress 2026 begins today at the Melaka International Trade Centre (MITC) in Ayer Keroh, Melaka, under the theme “Memugar Reformasi, Membina Madani” (Revitalising Reformasi, Building Madani).
The congress is seen as an important platform for the party to strengthen its direction while reinvigorating the spirit of the reformasi struggle that formed the foundation of PKR in navigating the current political landscape.
Anwar is scheduled to officiate the congress today and deliver his policy speech, which is expected to outline the party’s strategic agenda and direction. — Bernama

Title: PKR congress opens amid electoral setbacks and reformist departures
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 15 — Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) heads into its national congress this weekend facing a problem that goes beyond recent electoral defeats: convincing Malaysians that it still has something to fight for.
The party is grappling with the departure of prominent reformist figures, internal dissent and poor results in Sabah, Johor and Negeri Sembilan, with another state election in Melaka looming.
For a party built around reform, equal treatment and institutional change, its time in government has brought another challenge: convincing voters those ideals remain relevant after nearly four years in power.
International Islamic University Malaysia political scientist Associate Professor Syaza Shukri said must  determine its political direction while rebuilding public trust.
“I think the biggest issue would be how to go forward. I think PKR is at a crossroads especially after losing people like Rafizi and now Izzah taking leave. They need to figure out what’s the trajectory,” she said.
“If it’s still a reform agenda then how to proceed with that now that trust is low. How to win back people’s support rather than just uniting around the leadership.”
A year of upheaval
PKR’s troubles intensified after last year’s party election, when then-deputy president Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli lost the post to Nurul Izzah Anwar, daughter of party president and Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, by more than 5,900 votes.
Nurul Izzah secured 9,803 votes against Rafizi’s 3,866.
Rafizi subsequently resigned as economy minister, while Nik Nazmi Nik Ahmad left his Cabinet post as natural resources and environmental sustainability minister after failing to retain his vice-presidential position.
A year later, both men resigned as MPs and left PKR. In May this year, they took over the Malaysian United Party and rebranded it as Bersama, positioning it as a new multiracial political platform ahead of the next general election.
Their departure was followed by signs of sympathy within PKR, with several lawmakers attending Bersama’s launch. The new party did not make an electoral breakthrough in Johor, but its presence added another complication for Pakatan Harapan, which was already facing Barisan Nasional despite the two coalitions being federal government partners.
(From left) Nik Nazmi Nik Ahmad and Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli raise their hands together on stage during the official launch of the new political branding, Bersama, at the PJ Performing Arts Centre in Petaling Jaya on May 17, 2026. — Picture by Raymond Manuel
Three elections, three warnings
The electoral setbacks began in Sabah last November, where PKR won only one of the 12 seats it contested.
In Johor in July, PH won eight of the 56 state seats, down from 12 in 2022, with PKR securing only one through former education minister Maszlee Malik.
In Negeri Sembilan earlier this month, PH won 11 of the 36 seats and lost the state it had governed since 2018. PKR was reduced to two seats after losing four of its six incumbent constituencies.
The Negeri Sembilan result also highlighted the uneasy relationship between PH and BN, which contested separately while remaining federal government partners. BN subsequently worked with Perikatan Nasional in the state.
Syaza said the results should not automatically be read as PKR voters switching to rival parties, pointing instead to declining turnout, particularly among Chinese voters.
“Looking at recent elections, especially Johor and Negeri, it is not that PKR is losing support or support shifted to other parties. It’s just that a lot more people, especially Chinese voters, are choosing not to go out to vote,” she said.
“If that’s the case, the party needs to make a case to get them out, to mobilise them. And to do that the party needs to show it can fulfil the people’s expectations of PKR as the ruling party.”
Leadership and dissent
Questions over succession and dissent have also surfaced.
Nurul Izzah announced this month that she would step aside to pursue her studies. PKR subsequently granted her temporary leave, with vice-president Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail taking over her responsibilities.
Syaza said the episode highlighted PKR’s unresolved succession issue.
“It shows that the party has not settled the issue of succession and renewal and the next generation of leaders. It is still very Anwar-centric,” she said.
“So yes, now Amirudin is stepping up, but again it’s closing ranks behind Anwar’s faction with little dissent. That could both be good and bad. The party unites, but can it reinvigorate?”
Lee Chean Chung resigned from PKR’s central leadership council in June, saying the party was no longer what it was when he first joined.
Wong Chen then resigned as Subang MP earlier this week, ending his more than 10-year tenure in Parliament. He subsequently announced that he had left PKR and joined Bersama.
Wong, Lee and Ampang MP Rodziah Ismail have also raised concerns over their offices being blocked from accessing the MyKhas portal used to process constituency development allocations.
The dispute is politically sensitive for PKR, which has historically campaigned for equal allocations for elected representatives.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil has defended the government’s position, saying constituency allocations are at the Prime Minister’s discretion and should ultimately reach constituents rather than be treated as an entitlement of individual MPs.
Syaza said the controversy nevertheless carried a political cost.
“PKR used to fight for equal allocation and now this happens. It unfortunately shows the grassroots that firstly PKR doesn’t tolerate dissent and secondly it affects the whole reformist facade and idealism it once carried,” she said.
Wong Chen then resigned as Subang MP earlier this week, ending his more than 10-year tenure in Parliament. He subsequently announced that he had left PKR and joined Bersama.
What does PKR stand for now?
For Syaza, the deeper problem is the transformation that comes with being in government.
“Being in government has changed the party. On one hand that is fine. Of course we understand opposition and government are two different forms, one with resources, one without, one with access, one demanding access,” she said.
“But the problem now is people don’t even understand what PKR stands for anymore. It’s okay if as a government they say their means of reform might be different but that language is barely even there.”
She said the congress should reopen political space within the party and redefine what PKR could offer Malaysians.
“PKR needs to reopen political space. How can it be a reform party if it stifles different opinions? It doesn’t make sense,” she said.
“Secondly, redefine what it wants to give Malaysians. They’ve been in power and supporters have not been very happy so what else can they do and offer, realistically?”
“It’s no longer just about forming a government. They’ve had the chance. What else?”
Look forward, not back
Akademi Nusantara senior fellow Prof Azmi Hassan said delegates should focus on the party’s future rather than dwell on its recent setbacks.
“With all the setbacks PKR is facing right now, I think the delegates want to see something in the future. Let’s move forward,” he said.
Azmi said PKR should use its position in government to develop strategies before the next election, while cautioning against attributing all of PH’s recent losses to PKR.
“True enough, Sabah, Johor, Negeri Sembilan, it is a setback. But again, they have to look at their contest as a Pakatan Harapan using one symbol,” he said.
“Yes, PKR lost a lot of seats in Sabah, in Johor, and also in Negeri Sembilan, but maybe it is because of the Pakatan Harapan structure. Maybe it is because of one of their allies, DAP for example, that’s bringing down PKR in this case. That needs to be looked at during the congress itself.”
Azmi also defended the government’s position on constituency allocations, saying the funds were intended for constituencies rather than individual MPs.
“I agree with this allocation against constituencies for those MPs that are not with PKR. And I think Datuk Seri Anwar is correct that the allocation is not for the MP, but for the constituencies itself,” he said.
Melaka test looms
The next test will come in Melaka.
Azmi said PKR needed to demonstrate that it had learnt from its electoral setbacks in Sabah, Johor and Negeri Sembilan before the state goes to the polls.
“Looking at the next general election, I think PKR needs to make a lot of adjustments. They did not do enough after Sabah, after Johor, and Negeri Sembilan, and Melaka is coming very soon,” he said.
“I think there is time to do some tweaking in terms of making a better presentation to the people in the Melaka state election.”
PKR has signalled that its congress will focus on reforms, economic development and strengthening the party, according to vice-president Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari.
PH wrested Melaka from Barisan Nasional in 2018, ending decades of BN rule, but the administration collapsed in 2020 following the Sheraton Move, after which BN took back the state government.
For PKR, the question now is whether it can retain its reformist identity while governing, make greater room for dissent and give voters a compelling reason to return to the ballot box.

Title: Fadhlina urges PKR members to focus on ideas instead of exploiting religion
Article:
MELAKA, Aug 14 — Political competition should be based on ideas and the ability to offer the best solutions to the people, rather than exploiting matters of faith for political gain, said Wanita PKR chief Fadhlina Sidek.
She said religious issues should be respected and should not be exploited for political gain, particularly during elections.
“Do not incite people over matters of faith or exploit religion arbitrarily. We also believe that the space available is an opportunity for us to broaden and compete in terms of ideas, concepts, and who can offer better solutions.
“It should not be about campaigning by disparaging one another,” she said when delivering her winding-up speech at the 2026 Wanita PKR National Congress at the Melaka International Trade Centre in Ayer Keroh today.
Fadhlina also urged all PKR leaders and members to reconnect with the grassroots by strengthening ties with the people, including by understanding the community’s needs directly.
She said leaders at all levels of the party must be sensitive to the circumstances of the communities around them and take action to assist those in need.
“Look around your neighbours’ homes, as there may be many things that need our help. So, this is among the things that must also return to being our foundation with the people,” she said.
Fadhlina also reminded PKR members to remain loyal and steadfast in their commitment to the party’s struggle despite facing various trials and challenges.
She said the party’s strength must be built through hard work and the readiness of its machinery at all levels to ensure that the shared struggle with the people could continue.
“So, let’s continue our hard work, remain loyal, committed and confident in this struggle. Insya-Allah, I am very confident that we will do better,” she said. — Bernama

Title: Health minister warns contractors: Show progress or risk losing MOH projects
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 14 — The Ministry of Health (MOH) will not compromise on unreasonable delays in over 1,300 health facility development projects nationwide, and is prepared to terminate the contracts of contractors who fail to show convincing physical progress on-site.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said in a Facebook post today that such action is necessary to ensure planned projects are completed according to requirements so that the public can enjoy the benefits promptly, while also preventing the waste of public funds.
He noted that this matter was among those highlighted while chairing MOH’s Development Action Council (MTPK) Meeting No. 2 of 2026 this morning, which was also attended by representatives from the Public Works Department (JKR) and Finance Ministry.
Dzulkefly said that the MOH is also collaborating with the JKR, state governments, and utility companies to resolve issues affecting project implementation at the grassroots level.
In a related development, he said 10 major health facilities have been completed as of August, including the Northern Region Blood Centre in Kedah, the additional block of Tuanku Ampuan Najihah Hospital in Negeri Sembilan, and the Manjoi Klinik Kesihatan in Perak.
He also said that under the “Program Cakna Madani” initiative, 268 projects, or 37.75 per cent, have been completed, including improvements to the comfort of rural clinics, the expansion of haemodialysis centre capacities, and the replacement of obsolete equipment.
““Insya-Allah, I will ensure that every sen of the national health allocation is translated into a healthcare system that is more equitable, modern and comfortable for you all. Pray that our efforts are facilitated,” he added. — Bernama

Title: Thunderstorms, heavy rain ahead tonight for Selangor, Perak, Johor and four other states, MetMalaysia warns
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 14 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning for thunderstorms, heavy rain, and strong winds expected to affect seven states until 9pm today.
In a statement, MetMalaysia said the affected states are Perak (Bagan Datuk, Muallim, Hilir Perak, and Batang Padang), Terengganu, Pahang, and Johor (Mersing).
A similar warning was also issued for Selangor (Sepang, Klang, Sabak Bernam, Kuala Selangor, and Kuala Langat), Negeri Sembilan (Rembau and Port Dickson), and Melaka (Alor Gajah and Melaka Tengah). — Bernama

Title: KTMB adds 124 ETS, EMU Plus services, nearly 39,000 seats for National Day, school holidays
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 14 — Keretapi Tanah Melayu Berhad (KTMB) is adding 124 services with 38,944 seats for its Electric Train Service (ETS) and Electric Multiple Unit (EMU) Plus services during the upcoming National Day and school holidays.
In a statement today, KTMB said 100 additional ETS services, offering 31,600 seats, would operate over 10 days from August 21 to 23, August 28 to 31, and September 4 to 6.
“These initiatives are part of KTMB’s efforts to increase capacity, expand travel options and meet rising passenger demand, particularly during the holiday season and National Day celebrations,” it said.
Additionally, 24 extra EMU Plus services, offering a total of 7,344 seats, will operate on selected dates from August 21 to September 6, including an extension of services to Bandar Tasik Selatan.
For the KTM Komuter’s northern sector, eight additional services on the Padang Besar-Butterworth-Padang Besar route will operate from August 27 to 31, bringing the total to 46 services daily on the route.
The statement said tickets for the additional services went on sale yesterday through KTMB’s official sales channels.
Meanwhile, KTMB also held various customer appreciation activities from August 10 to 14, including vouchers, KFC meals, free travel tickets and RM16 discounts to mark the ETS’ 16th anniversary.
Its group chief executive officer Datuk Azlan Shah Al Bakri said the strong performance of ETS over its 16 years of operation reflected customers’ high confidence in the reliability of the country’s rail transport system.
“Starting in 2010 with the route to Ipoh, the ETS service was expanded to Butterworth and Padang Besar in 2015 before further expanding southwards at the end of 2025,” he said.
He said the ETS, introduced on August 12, 2010, had now recorded 44.3 million passengers, with statistics for January to July this year showing a 56 per cent increase to 3.67 million passengers from 2.36 million in the same period last year.
The development reflected KTMB’s commitment to providing wider, more comfortable and competitive rail services while continuing to improve capacity, service reliability and the passenger experience, he added. — Bernama

Title: Free rides are over: LRT3 Shah Alam Line passengers start paying tomorrow
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Aug 14 — After six weeks of enjoying free fares, passengers on the Light Rail Transit 3 (LRT3) Shah Alam Line will start to pay for their rides starting tomorrow (August 15).
Rapid KL in a statement announced that this includes the shuttle bus service as well as the Park N’ Ride facility.
“The implementation of this paid service marks another important phase in the operation of the Shah Alam Line after the six-week free travel period which was well received by the public.
“Rapid KL would like to express its gratitude to all users for their support, trust and willingness to choose public transport during the period,” the statement said.
Rapid KL also advised passengers to always prepare before starting their journey by ensuring their fare cards have at least RM5.
The public transport operator also informed that passengers can check the fare rates for the Shah Alam Line via the official MyRapid website.
“At the same time, concessionary fares via the MyRapid Concession Card are also available for eligible categories, including students, senior citizens and the disabled. Eligible passengers can use their respective concession cards to enjoy the set fare rates.
“Rapid KL welcomes the public to continue travelling with the Shah Alam Line and make public transport an option for easier, safer and smoother daily travel,” the statement said. — Bernama

Title: ‘Extraordinarily rash’: Prosecutor says police officer deliberately chased Ipoh teen before fatal crash
Article:
IPOH, Aug 14 — The High Court here was told today that the action of a senior police officer chasing a victim at high speed before crashing into him was described as a very dangerous act and showed “extraordinary rashness”.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Afzainizam Abdul Aziz in his rebuttal said that DSP Mohd Nazri Abdul Razak’s action of chasing Muhammad Zaharif Affendi Muhd Zamrie at close range was done with the knowledge that the act could result in death.
He said the accused was found not slowing down the Perodua Ativa he was driving even after passing a bump in the school area, but instead continued to follow closely before crashing into the victim at an intersection.
“The act by the accused was not only imminently dangerous, it is extraordinarily rash, it is crystal clear evidence of deliberate chase and tailgating by the accused against an unknown victim, a stranger, by following him closely after he left the school grounds.
“And when the accused got the opportunity, he hit him from the rear at the intersection, where the victim did not know that someone was actually behind him so close, chasing him,” he said.
Replying to doubts claimed by the defence, Afzainizam stressed that the absence of tyre tread marks on the victim’s body was not proof that the teenager had not been run over, instead citing the testimony of a pathologist that the thick clothing factor may have protected the marks although the possibility of the incident still exists.
Regarding the Event Data Recorder (EDR) data, Afzainizam said the speed and brake application information of the accused’s vehicle was obtained through special software by Perodua’s technical assistant who extracted the data without having to remove the hardware from the vehicle to maintain the integrity of the report analysis.
Judge Datuk Bhupindar Singh Gucharan Singh Preet set October 28 to decide whether Mohd Nazri, 46, should be called to defend himself on the charge of murdering Muhammad Zaharif Affendi, 17.
The prosecution was led by Afzainizam, assisted by Nasrul Hadi Abdul Ghani and Monisha Pandey, while the accused was represented by lawyers Datuk M. Athimulan, Datuk Mior Faridalathrash Wahid and Aiman Hakim Kamaruzzaman.
Mohd Nazri is charged with killing the teenager near Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan (SMK) Jati here, between 11.55am and 12.32pm, December 15, 2023.
The senior police officer is charged under Section 302 of the Penal Code which carries the death penalty or a minimum prison sentence of 30 to 40 years, and if not sentenced to death, he must be whipped not less than 12 strokes of the cane. — Bernama
